**Depends on:** `AXSECURITY`, `AXCIVIL`, `AXLAW`, `AXGOV`, `AXNETWORK`, `AXASSET`, `AXPROPERTY`

> Đây là **nâng cấp semantic của AXIDENTITY hiện hữu**, không tạo một identity system thứ hai. `AXIDENTITY` tiếp tục là nơi sở hữu identity facts và identity lifecycle; `AXSECURITY` sở hữu cryptographic trust, authentication primitives và authorization substrate.

# 728.0 — Mục tiêu

`AXIDENTITY 2.0` trở thành identity fabric dùng chung cho toàn bộ Axiom.

```text
                    AXIDENTITY
                         │
       ┌─────────────────┼──────────────────┐
       ↓                 ↓                  ↓
    Human             Organization       Device
       │                 │                  │
       └──────────────┬──┴──────────────────┘
                      ↓
                Identity Graph
                      ↓
              Claims / Credentials
                      ↓
                AXSECURITY
                      ↓
        Authentication / Authorization
```

Identity phải phân biệt rõ:

```text
identity
identifier
account
credential
authentication
authorization
role
attribute
claim
relationship
profile
legal status
device identity
service identity
```

```text
ID-INV-01   Every identity has a stable identity ID.
ID-INV-02   Identity IDs are independent of mutable profile data.
ID-INV-03   Identifier uniqueness scope is explicit.
ID-INV-04   Identity and account are distinct concepts.
ID-INV-05   Identity and credential are distinct concepts.
ID-INV-06   Authentication does not imply identity ownership.
ID-INV-07   Authentication does not imply authorization.
ID-INV-08   Identity lifecycle state is explicit.
ID-INV-09   Identity history cannot be silently rewritten.
ID-INV-10   Retired identity references remain resolvable when policy requires.

ID-INV-11   Identity relationships have explicit type.
ID-INV-12   Relationships have explicit validity.
ID-INV-13   Relationship provenance is preserved.
ID-INV-14   Delegation does not imply ownership.
ID-INV-15   Delegation cannot silently expand authority.
ID-INV-16   Identity merge preserves provenance.
ID-INV-17   Identity split preserves provenance.
ID-INV-18   Ambiguous identity resolution cannot silently select a candidate.
ID-INV-19   Probabilistic matching is distinguishable from authoritative resolution.
ID-INV-20   AI identity matching cannot directly create authoritative identity state.

ID-INV-21   Claims identify their issuer.
ID-INV-22   Credentials identify their subject.
ID-INV-23   Credential validity is independently verifiable.
ID-INV-24   Revoked credentials cannot be reported as valid.
ID-INV-25   Expired credentials cannot be reported as current.
ID-INV-26   Federation mappings have explicit trust policy.
ID-INV-27   External identity is not automatically local authority.
ID-INV-28   Identity assurance is explicit.
ID-INV-29   Offline verification exposes freshness.
ID-INV-30   Cached identity state is not automatically authoritative.

ID-INV-31   Identity references do not require duplicating identity profiles.
ID-INV-32   Identity deletion semantics distinguish retirement, anonymization, and destruction.
ID-INV-33   Privacy-preserving identifiers are scope-bound.
ID-INV-34   Pairwise identifiers cannot silently become global identifiers.
ID-INV-35   Sensitive identity attributes require explicit access policy.
ID-INV-36   Identity audit records preserve actor and event provenance.
ID-INV-37   Identity simulation cannot mutate production state.
ID-INV-38   Identity replay cannot create production side effects.
ID-INV-39   Civil/legal facts cannot be inferred solely from identity graph structure.
ID-INV-40   Identity security operations delegate cryptographic authority to AXSECURITY.
```

```text
AI-INV-19   Compilation artifacts identify their target environment.
AI-INV-20   Cached compiled artifacts are invalidated when compatibility changes.

AI-INV-21   Model architecture and model parameters are distinct.

AI-INV-23   Model lineage is preserved.
AI-INV-24   Dataset versions are identifiable.
AI-INV-25   Training runs identify model and dataset versions.

AI-INV-28   Deterministic runs record RNG state/configuration.
```

# 730.121 — Formal Invariants

```text
MED-INV-01   Container and codec are distinct concepts.
MED-INV-02   Stream and track are distinct concepts.
MED-INV-03   Packet and frame are distinct concepts.
MED-INV-04   Media timestamps use explicit timebases.
MED-INV-05   Authoritative timestamps do not use floating-point representation.
MED-INV-06   PTS and DTS remain distinguishable when applicable.
MED-INV-07   Audio sample rate is explicit.
MED-INV-08   Audio channel layout is explicit.
MED-INV-09   Video pixel format is explicit.
MED-INV-10   Video color metadata is explicit.

MED-INV-11   Frame rate uses exact rational representation.
MED-INV-12   Clock source is explicit.
MED-INV-13   Clock drift is measurable.
MED-INV-14   Synchronization policy is explicit.
MED-INV-15   Media pipeline preserves declared timing semantics.
MED-INV-16   Backpressure behavior is explicit.
MED-INV-17   Real-time pipelines have explicit latency/deadline policy.
MED-INV-18   Offline pipelines may not silently claim real-time guarantees.
MED-INV-19   Dropped frames are distinguishable from decoded frames.
MED-INV-20   Recovered/corrupted frames expose recovery state.

MED-INV-21   A media reference is independent of file path.
MED-INV-22   Published media versions are immutable.
MED-INV-23   Non-destructive edits preserve source references.
MED-INV-24   Timeline clips do not imply media duplication.
MED-INV-25   Smart rendering cannot alter unaffected source data.
MED-INV-26   Derived thumbnails/proxies are distinguishable from originals.
MED-INV-27   Cache data is never authoritative media state.
MED-INV-28   Metadata provenance is preserved.
MED-INV-29   AI-derived media metadata is distinguishable from source metadata.
MED-INV-30   Media processing provenance can be recorded.

MED-INV-31   Zero-copy operations preserve buffer ownership semantics.
MED-INV-32   Device-local buffers are not implicitly copied through host memory.
MED-INV-33   GPU processing may retain media buffers on device.
MED-INV-34   Hardware acceleration is capability-driven.
MED-INV-35   Unsupported codec operations are explicit failures.
MED-INV-36   Remuxing does not imply transcoding.
MED-INV-37   Transcoding does not silently claim bit-exact preservation.
MED-INV-38   Media replay cannot mutate source artifacts.
MED-INV-39   Media simulation cannot mutate production state.
MED-INV-40   Security and cryptographic authority remain outside AXMEDIA.
```

```text
GFX-INV-15   Shader stage is explicit.

GFX-INV-18   Render targets have explicit formats.
GFX-INV-19   Depth/stencil state is explicit.
GFX-INV-20   Blend state is explicit.

GFX-INV-21   Render graph dependencies are explicit.
GFX-INV-22   Render graph compilation preserves resource hazards.
GFX-INV-23   Transient resources cannot escape their declared lifetime.
GFX-INV-24   GPU-generated commands remain synchronized with consumers.
GFX-INV-25   Coordinate system convention is explicit.
GFX-INV-26   Camera projection parameters are explicit.
GFX-INV-27   Scene transforms preserve hierarchy semantics.
GFX-INV-28   Material data is distinct from shader executable code.
GFX-INV-29   Asset identity is distinct from GPU resource identity.
GFX-INV-30   GPU residency is distinguishable from logical resource existence.

GFX-INV-31   Dropped/evicted resources do not silently change logical asset identity.
GFX-INV-32   Shared media/AI/compute resources preserve synchronization semantics.
GFX-INV-33   Zero-copy paths preserve ownership.
GFX-INV-34   GPU acceleration cannot silently change declared numerical semantics.
GFX-INV-35   Deterministic mode records required execution parameters.
GFX-INV-36   Render replay does not mutate original scene state.
GFX-INV-37   Simulation does not mutate production GPU state.
GFX-INV-38   Debug instrumentation is separable from production hot paths.
```

# 732.181 — Formal Invariants

```text
UI-INV-01   UI node identity is stable within its lifetime.
UI-INV-02   Visual tree parent-child relationships are explicit.
UI-INV-03   Logical tree relationships are distinct from visual hierarchy.
UI-INV-04   A node cannot have two parents simultaneously.
UI-INV-05   Destroyed nodes cannot receive events.
UI-INV-06   Layout uses explicit measure and arrange semantics.
UI-INV-07   Logical units are distinct from physical pixels.
UI-INV-08   DPI scaling is explicit.
UI-INV-09   Hit testing respects transforms and clipping.
UI-INV-10   Event routing order is deterministic.

UI-INV-11   Pointer capture is explicit.
UI-INV-12   Focus ownership is explicit.
UI-INV-13   Text input is distinct from physical key events.
UI-INV-14   IME composition cannot be treated as ordinary committed text.
UI-INV-15   Selection state is explicit.
UI-INV-16   Clipboard operations are explicit.
UI-INV-17   Drag/drop operations declare allowed semantics.
UI-INV-18   Commands are distinct from visual controls.
UI-INV-19   UI visibility is not authorization.
UI-INV-20   UI validation is not domain validation.

UI-INV-21   Accessibility semantics are distinct from visual appearance.
UI-INV-22   Accessibility state is derived from authoritative UI state.
UI-INV-23   Localization does not mutate semantic identifiers.
UI-INV-24   RTL direction is explicit.
UI-INV-25   Unicode text semantics are preserved.
UI-INV-26   Theme is distinct from widget state.
UI-INV-27   Style resolution is deterministic.
UI-INV-28   Animation uses a monotonic clock.
UI-INV-29   Reduced-motion preferences are respected.
UI-INV-30   Virtualized controls preserve logical item identity.

UI-INV-31   UI mutations cannot race with protected UI-thread state.
UI-INV-32   Background work cannot directly mutate UI-owned state without synchronization.
UI-INV-33   Render snapshots are immutable during rendering.
UI-INV-34   UI rendering does not mutate logical application state.
UI-INV-35   Dropped frames cannot silently drop semantic events.
UI-INV-36   Resource destruction cannot occur while rendering uses the resource.
UI-INV-37   GPU resource synchronization is delegated to AXGRAPHICS.
UI-INV-38   Persistent state is distinct from transient UI state.
UI-INV-39   Replay does not mutate the original event log.
UI-INV-40   Simulation cannot mutate production UI state.
```

# 733.165 — Formal Invariants

```text
AUD-INV-01   Audio sample format is explicit.
AUD-INV-02   Sample rate is explicit.
AUD-INV-03   Channel layout is explicit.
AUD-INV-04   Frame is distinct from sample.
AUD-INV-05   Interleaved and planar layouts are distinguishable.
AUD-INV-06   Buffer duration derives from sample count and sample rate.
AUD-INV-07   Audio timestamps identify a clock domain.
AUD-INV-08   Sample position is monotonic within an audio clock.
AUD-INV-09   Clock conversion preserves provenance.
AUD-INV-10   Clock drift is distinguishable from timestamp offset.

AUD-INV-11   Resampling cannot silently alter logical duration.
AUD-INV-12   Channel conversion is explicit.
AUD-INV-13   Downmix coefficients are explicit.
AUD-INV-14   Gain semantics distinguish linear and decibel representations.
AUD-INV-15   DSP node state is distinct from input audio data.
AUD-INV-16   Real-time processing cannot require unbounded blocking.
AUD-INV-17   Real-time buffers have bounded capacity.
AUD-INV-18   Audio graph dependencies are explicit.
AUD-INV-19   Audio graph cycles require explicit delay/state semantics.
AUD-INV-20   Audio graph compilation preserves ordering requirements.

AUD-INV-21   Sample-accurate events use explicit sample positions.
AUD-INV-22   Automation is distinct from audio sample data.
AUD-INV-23   Device identity is distinct from physical asset identity.
AUD-INV-24   Device disconnect is an explicit state transition.
AUD-INV-25   Underrun and overrun are distinguishable.
AUD-INV-26   Recovery policy is explicit.
AUD-INV-27   Capture and playback streams have independent lifetimes.
AUD-INV-28   Duplex synchronization is explicit.
AUD-INV-29   Spatial source and listener transforms are explicit.
AUD-INV-30   Spatialization does not alter source identity.

AUD-INV-31   Audio AI results are derived data unless explicitly promoted by an authority.
AUD-INV-32   Audio fingerprints do not prove ownership.
AUD-INV-33   Cached audio data is not authoritative source state.
AUD-INV-34   Rendered/generated audio is distinct from source recording.
AUD-INV-35   Replay cannot mutate original audio state.
AUD-INV-36   Simulation cannot mutate production audio state.
AUD-INV-37   Security authorization remains outside audio semantics.
AUD-INV-38   Network transport semantics remain owned by AXNETWORK.
AUD-INV-39   Codec/container semantics remain owned by AXMEDIA.
AUD-INV-40   Deterministic mode records the configuration required for reproducible processing.
```

# 734.128 — Formal Invariants

```text
INP-INV-01   Every normalized event has an explicit event kind.
INP-INV-02   Every event has a timestamp.
INP-INV-03   Timestamp clock domain is explicit.
INP-INV-04   Device identity is distinct from OS handle.
INP-INV-05   Device identity is distinct from AXASSET identity.
INP-INV-06   Device lifecycle transitions are explicit.
INP-INV-07   Disconnect invalidates active device handles.
INP-INV-08   Raw events remain distinguishable from normalized events.
INP-INV-09   Physical keys remain distinguishable from logical keys.
INP-INV-10   Text input remains distinct from key events.

INP-INV-11   Touch identities are stable for a contact lifetime.
INP-INV-12   Pointer coordinates have explicit coordinate space.
INP-INV-13   Analog values retain source capability semantics.
INP-INV-14   Calibration is distinct from raw device state.
INP-INV-15   Dead-zone processing is a mapping operation.
INP-INV-16   Synthetic input carries explicit origin metadata.
INP-INV-17   Replay input remains distinguishable from live input.
INP-INV-18   Prediction is distinguishable from measurement.
INP-INV-19   Interpolation is distinguishable from measurement.
INP-INV-20   Input mappings are versionable.

INP-INV-21   Input context precedence is explicit.
INP-INV-22   Input capture is explicit.
INP-INV-23   Focus is distinct from device ownership.
INP-INV-24   Device assignment is distinct from identity authentication.
INP-INV-25   Input routing cannot silently bypass security policy.
INP-INV-26   Raw input access requires explicit capability.
INP-INV-27   Haptic output is distinct from input acquisition.
INP-INV-28   Gesture recognition produces derived events.
INP-INV-29   Sensor fusion produces derived observations.
INP-INV-30   AI-generated input is marked as AI-originated.

INP-INV-31   Input queue overflow behavior is explicit.
INP-INV-32   Real-time input paths cannot require unbounded blocking.
INP-INV-33   Event coalescing is distinguishable from raw event delivery.
INP-INV-34   Input snapshots have explicit temporal semantics.
INP-INV-35   Replay does not mutate the original recording.
INP-INV-36   Simulation cannot mutate production device state.
INP-INV-37   Security authorization belongs to AXSECURITY.
INP-INV-38   UI semantics belong above AXINPUT.
INP-INV-39   Physical device semantics are separated from logical actions.
INP-INV-40   Input provenance is preserved across normalization, mapping, replay, and synthesis.
```

# 735.160 — Formal Invariants

```text
UI-INV-01   Every UI element has stable identity.
UI-INV-02   UI identity is not a memory address.
UI-INV-03   Logical tree and visual tree are distinct concepts.
UI-INV-04   Accessibility tree is semantically independent.
UI-INV-05   Window lifecycle transitions are explicit.
UI-INV-06   Surface lifecycle is distinct from window lifecycle.
UI-INV-07   Layout operates on explicit constraints.
UI-INV-08   Layout invalidation is explicit.
UI-INV-09   Visual invalidation is distinct from layout invalidation.
UI-INV-10   Coordinate spaces are explicit.

UI-INV-11   Logical units are distinct from physical pixels.
UI-INV-12   Display scale is explicit.
UI-INV-13   UI supports multiple display contexts.
UI-INV-14   Text input is distinct from key input.
UI-INV-15   IME composition state is preserved.
UI-INV-16   Text layout supports Unicode semantics.
UI-INV-17   RTL direction is explicit.
UI-INV-18   Localization is distinct from rendering.
UI-INV-19   Clipboard data has explicit format.
UI-INV-20   Drag/drop payload has explicit action semantics.

UI-INV-21   Input routing follows explicit propagation phases.
UI-INV-22   Pointer capture is explicit.
UI-INV-23   Focus is distinct from pointer capture.
UI-INV-24   Modal scopes constrain event routing.
UI-INV-25   UI validation is distinct from domain validation.
UI-INV-26   UI state is distinct from application truth.
UI-INV-27   UI bindings are typed.
UI-INV-28   Binding updates are deterministic.
UI-INV-29   Commands are distinct from visual controls.
UI-INV-30   Undo history is distinct from domain transactions.

UI-INV-31   Accessibility semantics cannot depend solely on pixels.
UI-INV-32   Accessibility actions map to explicit UI capabilities.
UI-INV-33   Reduced-motion policy is respected by animation.
UI-INV-34   Sensitive input can be marked secure.
UI-INV-35   UI cannot bypass AXSECURITY authorization.
UI-INV-36   Native platform controls cannot redefine AXUI core semantics.
UI-INV-37   Immediate and retained UI modes share core event semantics.
UI-INV-38   Virtualized controls cannot require materialization of all items.
UI-INV-39   AI-generated UI is explicitly attributable.
UI-INV-40   UI replay and simulation cannot silently mutate production state.
```

```text
WIN-INV-12   Display scale is explicit.
WIN-INV-13   Per-display scale changes are observable.
WIN-INV-14   Display topology is versionable.
WIN-INV-15   Display removal is observable.

WIN-INV-17   Display mode changes are capability-checked.
WIN-INV-18   Fullscreen state is distinct from ordinary window size.
WIN-INV-19   Borderless fullscreen is distinct from exclusive fullscreen.
WIN-INV-20   Refresh rate is represented without lossy floating-point canonicalization.

WIN-INV-22   HDR capability is distinct from HDR rendering.
WIN-INV-23   VRR capability is distinct from frame scheduling.
WIN-INV-24   Presentation is distinct from rendering command generation.
WIN-INV-25   Window surfaces can be recreated without necessarily changing window identity.
WIN-INV-26   Native handles are opaque and backend-specific.
WIN-INV-27   Native handles have explicit lifetime semantics.
WIN-INV-28   Window manager changes are treated as external state changes.
WIN-INV-29   Platform policy can reject requested window operations.
WIN-INV-30   AXWINDOW cannot bypass platform security policy.

WIN-INV-32   Raw input belongs to AXINPUT.
WIN-INV-33   GPU rendering belongs to AXGRAPHICS.
WIN-INV-34   Audio lifecycle signals do not make AXWINDOW an audio subsystem.
WIN-INV-35   Display capture is distinct from display rendering.
WIN-INV-36   Cross-process window access requires explicit capability.
WIN-INV-37   Synthetic input injection is not implicit in window ownership.
WIN-INV-38   Headless surfaces cannot require a physical display.
```

# 737.151 — Formal Invariants

```text
DSP-INV-01   Every display has an explicit display identity.
DSP-INV-02   Physical and logical display identities are distinct.
DSP-INV-03   Display output identity is distinct from panel identity.
DSP-INV-04   Display controller identity is distinct from output identity.
DSP-INV-05   Display topology is versioned.
DSP-INV-06   Display connection state is observable.
DSP-INV-07   Display disconnection is observable.
DSP-INV-08   Display resolution is represented in integer pixels.
DSP-INV-09   Native resolution is distinct from active resolution.
DSP-INV-10   Display mode is explicit.

DSP-INV-11   Refresh rate uses lossless rational representation.
DSP-INV-12   VRR capability is distinct from active VRR state.
DSP-INV-13   VSync capability is distinct from frame scheduling policy.
DSP-INV-14   Display timing has an explicit clock domain.
DSP-INV-15   Presentation timestamps identify their timing domain.
DSP-INV-16   Cross-display synchronization is explicit.
DSP-INV-17   Display scale is distinct from physical pixel density.
DSP-INV-18   DPI type is explicit.
DSP-INV-19   Display coordinate space is explicit.
DSP-INV-20   Coordinate transformations are explicit.

DSP-INV-21   Color space is distinct from pixel format.
DSP-INV-22   HDR capability is distinct from HDR activation.
DSP-INV-23   HDR metadata is distinct from HDR pixel data.
DSP-INV-24   Color profile provenance is preserved.
DSP-INV-25   Calibration provenance is preserved.
DSP-INV-26   Brightness semantics are explicit.
DSP-INV-27   Display power state is observable.
DSP-INV-28   Display power control is permission-aware.
DSP-INV-29   Orientation is distinct from content rotation.
DSP-INV-30   Physical and logical rotation are distinct.

DSP-INV-31   Display configuration is transactional where backend permits.
DSP-INV-32   Requested configuration is distinct from actual configuration.
```

```text
UI-INV-01   Every UI node has a stable runtime identity.
UI-INV-02   UI identity is distinct from memory address.
UI-INV-03   Visual tree hierarchy is explicit.
UI-INV-04   Node ownership is explicit.

UI-INV-08   Accessibility tree is distinct from visual tree.

UI-INV-14   Event propagation order is deterministic.
UI-INV-15   Event consumption is explicit.

UI-INV-17   UI coordinate spaces are explicit.
UI-INV-18   Logical units are distinct from physical pixels.
UI-INV-19   Display scale is not silently treated as DPI.
UI-INV-20   Layout invalidation is explicit.

UI-INV-21   Measure and arrange are distinct phases.
UI-INV-22   Layout may be incremental.
UI-INV-23   Layout results may be cached only while dependencies remain valid.
UI-INV-24   Style resolution is versioned.
UI-INV-25   Shared styles do not require per-node duplication.
UI-INV-26   Theme identity is explicit.
UI-INV-27   Theme changes invalidate dependent style state.
UI-INV-28   Text uses Unicode-aware semantics.
UI-INV-29   Byte offsets are distinct from text character semantics.
UI-INV-30   Visual glyph order is distinct from logical text order.

UI-INV-31   Accessibility semantics are explicit.
UI-INV-32   Accessibility focus may differ from keyboard focus.
UI-INV-33   UI automation identities are stable.
UI-INV-34   Virtualized collections need not instantiate every logical item.
UI-INV-35   UI updates may be coalesced without losing required semantic events.
UI-INV-36   Background work cannot silently mutate UI state outside the UI execution context.
UI-INV-37   AI-generated UI is untrusted until validated and authorized.
```

```text
DSK-INV-12   Multi-display placement is display-aware.
DSK-INV-13   Shared and independent workspace policies are explicit.
DSK-INV-14   Tiling layout state is deterministic.
DSK-INV-15   Snap preview cannot silently mutate committed placement.
DSK-INV-16   Panel identity is stable.
DSK-INV-17   Dock/taskbar semantics are distinct from generic panels.
DSK-INV-18   Application identity is distinct from executable path.
DSK-INV-19   Window identity is distinct from application identity.
DSK-INV-20   Window groups have explicit membership.

DSK-INV-21   Notification identity is stable.
DSK-INV-22   Notification actions require explicit capability.
DSK-INV-23   Lock-screen surfaces are isolated from normal application surfaces.
DSK-INV-24   Desktop unlock requires security authority.
DSK-INV-25   Global shortcuts require explicit authorization.
DSK-INV-26   Remote desktop input is capability-controlled.
DSK-INV-27   Remote observation cannot bypass capture policy.
DSK-INV-28   Session state cannot cross users without explicit authorization.
DSK-INV-29   Persistent desktop state is versioned.
DSK-INV-30   Desktop state commits are atomic.

DSK-INV-31   Crash recovery uses committed state only.
DSK-INV-32   Session restore is distinct from event replay.
DSK-INV-33   Replay does not mutate production desktop state.
DSK-INV-34   Simulation does not mutate production desktop state.

DSK-INV-37   Desktop hot paths do not require database access.
DSK-INV-38   Event coalescing cannot violate required lifecycle semantics.
```

# 745.201 — Formal Invariants

```text id="b0a5lq"
MEM-INV-01   Every memory region has a stable logical identity.
MEM-INV-02   Region identity is distinct from virtual address.
MEM-INV-03   Virtual addresses are scoped to an address space.
MEM-INV-04   Physical memory is not directly accessible by normal applications.
MEM-INV-05   Cross-process mappings require explicit authority.
MEM-INV-06   Memory protection is explicit.
MEM-INV-07   Executable writable memory obeys explicit W^X policy.
MEM-INV-08   Unmapped memory cannot be accessed as valid memory.
MEM-INV-09   Mapping granularity is explicit.
MEM-INV-10   Page size is a backend capability, not a language constant.

MEM-INV-11   Allocation identity is distinct from virtual address.
MEM-INV-12   Allocations have explicit lifetime semantics.
MEM-INV-13   Default allocation does not imply garbage collection.
MEM-INV-14   Arena allocations cannot outlive their arena.
MEM-INV-15   Pool allocations cannot outlive their owning pool.
MEM-INV-16   Raw pointers do not imply ownership.
MEM-INV-17   Non-owning views cannot extend backing-memory lifetime.
MEM-INV-18   Reallocation invalidates old pointers when relocation occurs.
MEM-INV-19   Stable-address memory cannot silently relocate.
MEM-INV-20   Relocatable memory must use an abstraction compatible with relocation.

MEM-INV-21   Shared memory mappings preserve explicit ownership/authority semantics.
MEM-INV-22   Zero-copy transfer preserves buffer lifetime.
MEM-INV-23   DMA memory has explicit device ownership semantics.
MEM-INV-24   Pinned memory is accounted against explicit resource limits.
MEM-INV-25   Device memory is distinct from ordinary host memory.
MEM-INV-26   NUMA placement is a policy, not an ownership mechanism.
MEM-INV-27   Memory migration preserves logical contents and permissions.
MEM-INV-28   Memory compaction cannot move arbitrary pointer-visible allocations.
MEM-INV-29   Copy-on-write preserves logical isolation.
MEM-INV-30   Memory aliases have explicit mapping semantics.

MEM-INV-31   Secure memory cannot be exposed through unauthorized mappings.
MEM-INV-32   Zeroization has observable security semantics.
MEM-INV-33   Physical/MMIO mapping requires privileged authority.
MEM-INV-34   Allocation failure is representable as explicit runtime state.
MEM-INV-35   Memory quota cannot be silently exceeded.
MEM-INV-36   Reclamation cannot discard live non-reclaimable allocations.
MEM-INV-37   Disabled diagnostics cannot require full debug overhead.
MEM-INV-38   Deterministic allocation is isolated from production allocation policy.
MEM-INV-39   Memory accounting is attributable to explicit ownership domains.
MEM-INV-40   Identical deterministic allocation inputs produce identical logical allocation state.
```

# 746.200 — Formal Invariants

```text
IPC-INV-01   Every endpoint has a unique logical identity within its namespace.
IPC-INV-02   Endpoint identity is distinct from memory address.
IPC-INV-03   Endpoint access requires explicit authority.
IPC-INV-04   A raw pointer cannot be transferred as a valid cross-process reference.
IPC-INV-05   Every message has an explicit type/layout.
IPC-INV-06   Message size is validated before payload access.
IPC-INV-07   Native IPC does not require runtime reflection.
IPC-INV-08   Local native messages need not be serialized.
IPC-INV-09   Remote messages cross an explicit wire-format boundary.
IPC-INV-10   Unknown protocol versions are handled explicitly.

IPC-INV-11   Queue capacity is finite unless explicit dynamic-growth policy exists.
IPC-INV-12   Reliable channels do not silently drop messages.
IPC-INV-13   Best-effort channels explicitly declare loss semantics.
IPC-INV-14   Backpressure behavior is explicit.
IPC-INV-15   Queue ownership is attributable to a resource domain.
IPC-INV-16   In-flight buffers retain valid lifetime ownership.
IPC-INV-17   Zero-copy transfer preserves buffer validity.
IPC-INV-18   Handle transfer preserves rights constraints.
IPC-INV-19   Capability delegation cannot increase authority.
IPC-INV-20   Closed endpoints reject new operations.

IPC-INV-21   Peer termination produces explicit endpoint/request state.
IPC-INV-22   Cancellation cannot retroactively change an already completed operation.
IPC-INV-23   Request IDs distinguish concurrent requests.
IPC-INV-24   Automatic retry requires explicit retry/idempotency semantics.
IPC-INV-25   Exactly-once application semantics are not assumed by default.
IPC-INV-26   Pending requests cannot exceed configured resource limits.
IPC-INV-27   Endpoint quotas cannot be silently exceeded.
IPC-INV-28   Shared-memory mappings require explicit security authority.
IPC-INV-29   Protected payloads are not automatically copied into diagnostics.
IPC-INV-30   IPC cannot bypass AXSECURITY authorization.

IPC-INV-31   IPC does not grant authority merely by message content.
IPC-INV-32   Capability-bearing messages preserve attenuation semantics.
IPC-INV-33   Confused-deputy-sensitive operations preserve caller authority context.
IPC-INV-34   Remote IPC requires an explicit network/security boundary.
IPC-INV-35   IPC tracing must be separable from production hot-path semantics.
IPC-INV-36   Deterministic replay is distinct from hardware-level execution determinism.
IPC-INV-37   Simulation faults cannot silently alter production security policy.
IPC-INV-38   Message ordering is defined by channel contract.
IPC-INV-39   Transport optimization cannot change logical IPC semantics.
IPC-INV-40   IPC fast paths must not require mandatory allocation, reflection, or global locking.
```

```text
SYNC-INV-01   Every synchronization object has a stable logical identity.
SYNC-INV-02   Atomic operations obey the declared memory-order semantics.
SYNC-INV-03   Atomic alignment requirements are respected.
SYNC-INV-04   Atomicity does not imply memory ownership.
SYNC-INV-05   Relaxed operations do not implicitly create acquire/release ordering.
SYNC-INV-06   Acquire operations cannot be weakened without changing semantics.
SYNC-INV-07   Release operations cannot be reordered past their synchronization boundary.
SYNC-INV-08   Sequential consistency is stronger than relaxed/acquire/release ordering.
SYNC-INV-09   Atomic wait observes the specified atomic state.
SYNC-INV-10   Wake operations cannot grant ownership by themselves.

SYNC-INV-11   Mutex ownership is exclusive.
SYNC-INV-12   A mutex cannot be unlocked by a non-owner under ownership-enforcing semantics.
SYNC-INV-13   Destroying an actively owned mutex is invalid.
SYNC-INV-14   Condition-variable wake does not imply predicate truth.
SYNC-INV-15   Semaphore permits cannot become negative.
SYNC-INV-16   Event reset semantics are explicit.
SYNC-INV-17   Barrier completion requires the declared participant condition.
SYNC-INV-18   Latch completion occurs only when its counter reaches zero.
SYNC-INV-19   Once initialization cannot execute concurrently more than once.
SYNC-INV-20   Timed waits use a defined monotonic deadline domain.

SYNC-INV-21   Shared synchronization objects require valid shared-memory lifetime.
SYNC-INV-22   Process-shared synchronization cannot bypass AXSECURITY.
SYNC-INV-23   Owner-death state is explicit when supported.
SYNC-INV-24   Robust recovery cannot silently assume shared-state consistency.
SYNC-INV-25   Forced thread termination does not implicitly repair arbitrary locks.
SYNC-INV-26   Cancellation cannot silently leave synchronization ownership inconsistent.
SYNC-INV-27   Waiters observe valid object lifetime.
SYNC-INV-28   Wakeups cannot access destroyed wait state.
SYNC-INV-29   Lock-free claims require a valid progress guarantee.
SYNC-INV-30   Wait-free claims require a bounded per-operation progress guarantee.

SYNC-INV-31   Lock-free reclamation cannot free an object still reachable by a protected reader.
SYNC-INV-32   Shared memory does not imply synchronization.
SYNC-INV-33   Synchronization does not automatically transfer memory ownership.
SYNC-INV-34   Data-race diagnostics do not alter production semantics.
```

# 748.200 — Formal Invariants

```text
TASK-INV-01   Every task has a unique logical identity.
TASK-INV-02   Task identity is distinct from worker-thread identity.
TASK-INV-03   Creating a task does not implicitly require creating an OS thread.
TASK-INV-04   A task has exactly one terminal completion state.
TASK-INV-05   A promise cannot complete more than once.
TASK-INV-06   Future observation synchronizes with published task result.
TASK-INV-07   Ready tasks cannot be silently lost from scheduler queues.
TASK-INV-08   Suspended tasks retain all state required for valid continuation.
TASK-INV-09   Task migration does not invalidate task-local state.
TASK-INV-10   Task handles cannot resolve to a recycled task without generation validation.

TASK-INV-11   Structured child tasks remain associated with their owning task group.
TASK-INV-12   A structured task group cannot complete before its required children reach terminal/group-defined states.
TASK-INV-13   Detached tasks require explicit detached ownership/supervision.
TASK-INV-14   Child failure propagation follows the declared group policy.
TASK-INV-15   Cancellation is a request unless an explicit stronger contract exists.
TASK-INV-16   Cancellation cannot retroactively change a completed task into CANCELLED.
TASK-INV-17   Child cancellation cannot implicitly cancel its parent.
TASK-INV-18   Parent cancellation may propagate to descendants according to scope policy.
TASK-INV-19   A deadline cannot be silently extended by a child task.
TASK-INV-20   Retry requires an explicit retry/idempotency policy.

TASK-INV-21   Awaiting a task in async context does not block the worker thread.
TASK-INV-22   Blocking operations execute on an appropriate blocking executor when required.
TASK-INV-23   Task synchronization uses AXSYNC primitives rather than hidden global locks.
TASK-INV-24   Async synchronization ownership is distinct from OS-thread synchronization ownership.
TASK-INV-25   Task frame lifetime remains valid while an escaping continuation can execute.
TASK-INV-26   Task frame reclamation cannot occur while a valid handle or continuation still references it.
TASK-INV-27   Work stealing cannot execute a task concurrently on two workers unless explicitly designed for concurrent execution.
TASK-INV-28   Scheduler queue operations preserve task ownership/lifetime.
TASK-INV-29   Scheduler migration preserves task semantics.
TASK-INV-30   Worker shutdown does not silently discard owned tasks.

TASK-INV-31   Task priority cannot bypass AXSECURITY authority.
TASK-INV-32   Realtime task priority cannot be granted without required system policy.
TASK-INV-33   Task context propagation cannot increase security authority.
TASK-INV-34   Task checkpoints cannot restore unauthorized capabilities.
TASK-INV-35   Replay does not imply exact hardware timing determinism.
TASK-INV-36   Diagnostic instrumentation cannot alter correctness semantics.
TASK-INV-37   Task tracing cannot automatically expose protected payload data.
TASK-INV-38   AI task analysis cannot bypass runtime security boundaries.
TASK-INV-39   Scheduler optimization cannot violate task deadlines/affinity contracts that are declared hard constraints.
TASK-INV-40   Uncontended task/future operations must avoid unnecessary heap allocation, kernel transitions, and global synchronization.
```

# 750.1 — Purpose

```text
Axiom source

object file
      ↓
static library / dynamic library
      ↓
executable / application
      ↓
```

**ABI là contract machine-level, không phải language-level syntax.**

# 751.377 — Formal Invariants

```text
MOD-INV-01   Every module has a deterministic canonical identity.
MOD-INV-02   Module identity is independent of filesystem path.
MOD-INV-03   Package identity and module identity are distinct.
MOD-INV-04   Interface and implementation are distinct artifacts/concepts.
MOD-INV-05   Every module dependency has explicit identity and version constraints.
MOD-INV-06   ABI compatibility is checked independently of semantic version compatibility.
MOD-INV-07   Dependency resolution is deterministic.
MOD-INV-08   Conflicting dependencies are never silently selected arbitrarily.
MOD-INV-09   Required dependencies must resolve before module activation.
MOD-INV-10   Optional dependencies cannot silently become required dependencies.

MOD-INV-11   Exported symbols have explicit ownership.
MOD-INV-12   Duplicate canonical symbol ownership is rejected.
MOD-INV-13   Re-export does not create a second type identity.
MOD-INV-14   Private implementation details are not automatically public ABI.
MOD-INV-15   Interface fingerprints change when ABI-relevant public contracts change.
MOD-INV-16   ABI fingerprints are delegated to AXABI's canonical rules.
MOD-INV-17   Target-specific variants are selected deterministically.
MOD-INV-18   Unsupported target variants fail before native linking.
MOD-INV-19   Static and dynamic linkage preserve declared ABI semantics.
MOD-INV-20   Native executable generation does not require a VM.

MOD-INV-21   Cached artifacts are reused only when all relevant fingerprints match.
MOD-INV-22   Dependency interface changes invalidate affected consumers.
MOD-INV-23   Private implementation changes do not unnecessarily invalidate unrelated consumers.
MOD-INV-24   Compiler-generated metadata is derived from canonical project/module state.
MOD-INV-25   Reproducible module identity cannot depend on timestamps or absolute paths.
MOD-INV-26   Precompiled interfaces cannot be loaded with incompatible format versions.
MOD-INV-27   Precompiled native artifacts cannot bypass ABI validation.
MOD-INV-28   Static library symbol indexing cannot change semantic symbol ownership.
MOD-INV-29   Dead-code elimination cannot remove required initialization side effects.
MOD-INV-30   Link plans are deterministic for identical resolved inputs.

MOD-INV-31   Dynamic module activation completes validation before services become visible.
MOD-INV-32   A failed module initialization cannot publish an ACTIVE module.
MOD-INV-33   A module cannot be unloaded while live execution state references its code.
MOD-INV-34   Async frames cannot outlive module code they reference.
MOD-INV-35   Module shutdown must quiesce declared services before unload.
MOD-INV-36   Module loading cannot grant security authority.
MOD-INV-37   Untrusted modules cannot bypass AXSECURITY policy.
MOD-INV-38   Malformed module metadata must be rejected without unsafe memory access.
MOD-INV-39   AI tooling cannot bypass dependency, ABI, or security validation.
MOD-INV-40   Every supported module format has mechanically testable validation rules.
```

# 751.398 — Critical Architectural Decision

Axiom sẽ **không biến module thành một runtime object bắt buộc**.

Có hai chế độ hoàn toàn hợp lệ:

### Static native

```text
Axiom source
 → modules
 → objects
 → linker
 → PE64/ELF/Mach-O/WASM
```

Sau link, module abstraction có thể biến mất hoàn toàn.

### Dynamic native

```text
Executable
 ↓
dynamic loader
 ↓
module metadata
 ↓
library/plugin
```

Module runtime chỉ tồn tại khi application thực sự cần dynamic loading.

Điều này giữ được mục tiêu **binary nhỏ + native performance cao** của Axiom.

## 1. Mục tiêu

`AXASYNC` là tầng runtime native chịu trách nhiệm cho **asynchronous I/O thực sự**, nằm giữa các resource subsystem (`AXSTORAGE`, `AXNETWORK`, `AXIPC`, device I/O...) và `AXTASK`.

Mục tiêu chính:

- asynchronous file I/O;
- asynchronous network I/O;
- asynchronous IPC integration;
- device/DMA I/O;
- OS completion ports;
- readiness polling;
- completion queues;
- timers;
- event sources;
- cancellation;
- deadlines;
- scatter/gather;
- zero-copy;
- registered/pinned buffers;
- batching;
- syscall minimization;
- tracing;
- deterministic simulation;
- fault injection;
- native cross-platform backend.

**Nguyên tắc nền tảng:**

> `AXASYNC` không phải async language runtime. Nó là **I/O completion substrate**.

`AXTASK` quyết định **task nào đang chạy**.

`AXASYNC` quyết định **I/O nào đã sẵn sàng hoặc đã hoàn thành**.

# 5. Hai mô hình async cơ bản

## 5.1 Readiness-based I/O

OS báo:

```text
"Resource này hiện có thể thực hiện I/O."
```

Ví dụ:

```text
READABLE
WRITABLE
ACCEPTABLE
ERROR
HANGUP
```

Sau đó application thực hiện operation.

Flow:

```text
poller
   │
   ▼
READABLE
   │
   ▼
application
   │
   ▼
read()
   │
   ▼
result
```

Readiness **không có nghĩa I/O đã hoàn thành**.

---

# 6. Completion-based I/O

OS/device thực hiện operation và trả về completion.

```text
submit(read)
      │
      ▼
   kernel
      │
      ▼
device
      │
      ▼
 completion
```

Application không cần thực hiện `read()` lần thứ hai.

Ví dụ:

```text
read_async(file, buffer, ...)
        │
        ▼
      submit
        │
        ▼
      kernel
        │
        ▼
    completion
        │
        ▼
      future
```

---

Hoặc:

> mọi I/O phải chạy qua io_uring.

```text
     ▼
Backend Capability Profile

 ┌───┼────┬─────┬─────┐
 ▼   ▼    ▼     ▼     ▼
IOCP io_uring kqueue WASM embedded
```

Các primitive chính:

```text
io_context
```

# 10. `io_operation`

Đây là object trung tâm.

```text
io_operation {
    request_id
    operation_kind
    source
    handle
    buffer
    offset
    length

    deadline
    cancellation

    flags
    user_data
    task_context

    state
}
```

Không yêu cầu heap allocation bắt buộc.

Runtime phải hỗ trợ operation object nằm:

```text
task frame
stack
slab
preallocated pool
```

---

# 11. Request ID

`io_request_id` không được đơn thuần là pointer.

Mô hình:

```text
request_id {
    index
    generation
}
```

Ví dụ:

```text
index = 381
generation = 17
```

Completion cũ:

```text
381:16
```

không thể nhầm với operation mới:

```text
381:17
```

Điều này bảo vệ chống **stale completion**.

---

# 12. Operation lifecycle

Canonical lifecycle:

```text
CREATED
   │
   ▼
SUBMITTED
   │
   ▼
IN_FLIGHT
   │
   ├──────────────► COMPLETED
   │
   ├──────────────► FAILED
   │
   ├──────────────► CANCEL_REQUESTED
   │                       │
   │                       ▼
   │                   CANCELLED
   │
   └──────────────► EXPIRED
```

`CANCEL_REQUESTED` **không đồng nghĩa** `CANCELLED`.

---

# 13. Completion record

```text
io_completion {
    request_id
    status
    bytes_transferred
    native_error
    timestamp
    flags
    user_data
}
```

Axiom giữ:

```text
stable error class
+
native OS error
```

Ví dụ:

```text
status = PERMISSION_DENIED
native_error = ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED
```

---

# 14. Completion guarantee

Mặc định:

> Một operation có đúng một terminal completion.

Trừ khi operation khai báo:

```text
PARTIAL_COMPLETION
MULTI_COMPLETION
STREAM_COMPLETION
```

Điều này giúp `future<T>` không bị double-complete.

---

# 15. Completion queue

```text
completion_queue
```

phải hỗ trợ:

```text
push()
pop()
poll()
wait()
drain()
drain_batch()
```

Batch:

```text
drain_batch(max = 64)
```

cho phép giảm syscall và scheduling overhead.

---

# 16. MPSC completion

Nhiều producer có thể hoàn thành I/O:

```text
worker 0 ─┐
worker 1 ─┤
worker 2 ─┼──► completion_queue
worker 3 ─┘
```

Consumer có thể là:

```text
một worker
hoặc nhiều worker
```

Không yêu cầu completion phải quay về đúng thread submit.

---

# 17. Wake coalescing

Không đánh thức worker cho từng completion nếu không cần.

Ví dụ:

```text
completion 1
completion 2
completion 3
completion 4
      │
      ▼
  one wakeup
      │
      ▼
 drain_batch(64)
```

Đây là một optimization quan trọng.

---

# 18. Polling API

```text
poller.poll()
poller.wait()
poller.poll_until(deadline)
poller.drain_completions()
```

Semantics:

### `poll`

Không block.

### `wait`

Có thể block thread.

### `poll_until`

Block tối đa đến deadline.

---

# 19. Worker parking

Mặc định:

```text
no completion
     │
     ▼
park worker
```

Không được busy-spin vô hạn.

Low-latency profile có thể cho phép:

```text
spin
→ short pause
→ park
```

nhưng đây phải là policy explicit.

---

# 20. Integration với AXTASK

Đây là đường đi canonical:

```text
async function read_file() {
    result = await file.read(buffer)
}
```

Compiler hạ xuống:

```text
AXTASK state machine
        │
        ▼
AXASYNC submit
        │
        ▼
suspend task
        │
        ▼
I/O completion
        │
        ▼
resume task
```

Worker thread không bị block.

---

# 21. Completion → Future

Completion token phải map được trực tiếp tới:

```text
future<T>
```

mà không bắt buộc allocation mới.

Ví dụ:

```text
io_request_id
      │
      ▼
task frame
      │
      ▼
future state
```

```text

write_async()
```

Result:

```text
{
```

Không giả định:

```text
requested = 4096
completed = 4096
```

Có thể:

```text
requested = 4096
completed = 1792
```

```text

    [

        buffer_c
```

```text

```

# 25. Scatter/Gather

Mỗi entry:

Nhưng semantics thuộc backend + AXSTORAGE.

Direct I/O phải khai báo:

```text
alignment
sector size
buffer constraints
offset constraints
```

Không tự động giả vờ rằng mọi platform hỗ trợ giống nhau.

---

# 27. Append semantics

`append` phải được biểu diễn bằng operation semantic rõ ràng.

Không làm:

```text
get_file_size()
write_at(size)
```

vì hai operation riêng biệt có race.

Backend phải cung cấp atomic append nếu platform hỗ trợ.

# 28. Network I/O

API:

```text
accept_async()
connect_async()
recv_async()
send_async()

recv_from_async()
send_to_async()
```

AXASYNC không sở hữu protocol.

Ví dụ:

```text
TCP
QUIC
UDP
```

---

# 29. Readiness socket

API:

```text
wait_readable()
wait_writable()
```

Flow:

```text
wait_readable()
      │
      ▼
READABLE
      │
      ▼
recv()
```

Đây khác hoàn toàn:

```text

      │
      ▼
completion
```

# 30. Ordering

Không mặc định rằng mọi request hoàn thành theo thứ tự submit.

Ví dụ:

```text
submit A
submit B
submit C

completion:
B
C
A
```

Được phép.

Nếu application yêu cầu ordering:

```text
ORDERED
```

phải khai báo explicit.

---

# 31. Per-stream ordering

Một stream có thể yêu cầu:

```text
A → B → C
```

Nhưng các stream độc lập:

```text
stream 1
stream 2
stream 3
```

có thể chạy song song.

Không áp dụng global ordering.

# 32. IPC integration

`AXASYNC` không tạo message model mới.

Nó chỉ cung cấp async transport.

```text
AXIPC endpoint
      │
      ▼
AXASYNC
      │
      ▼
completion
```

Ví dụ:

```text
await endpoint.receive_async()
```

message semantics vẫn thuộc `AXIPC`.

---

# 33. Shared-memory IPC

Với buffer lớn:

```text
AXMEMORY shared region
          │
          ▼
       AXIPC
          │
          ▼
      AXASYNC
```

Không copy payload nếu transport hỗ trợ ownership transfer.

---

# 34. Zero-copy

Mục tiêu:

```text
device
  ↓
registered buffer
  ↓
application
```

thay vì:

```text
device
  ↓
kernel buffer
  ↓
temporary buffer
  ↓
application buffer
```

Zero-copy chỉ được tuyên bố khi backend thực sự đáp ứng semantic tương ứng.

---

# 35. Registered buffer

API:

```text
register_buffer()
unregister_buffer()
```

Buffer phải thuộc `AXMEMORY`.

Lifecycle:

```text
ALLOCATED
    ↓
REGISTERED
    ↓
IN_USE
    ↓
AVAILABLE
    ↓
RELEASED
```

Không được release buffer khi operation còn `IN_FLIGHT`.

---

# 36. Buffer group

```text
io_buffer_group
```

cho phép preallocate:

```text
N × fixed-size buffers
```

Backend lấy buffer từ pool.

Ví dụ:

```text
64 × 64 KiB
```

rất phù hợp server/network workloads.

---

# 37. Buffer ownership

Một buffer có ownership state:

```text
APPLICATION
KERNEL
DEVICE
TRANSFERRED
```

Không cho phép hai owner ghi đồng thời nếu không có explicit shared semantics.

---

# 38. DMA

DMA buffer phải khai báo:

```text
PINNED
DEVICE_VISIBLE
CACHE_COHERENT
```

Nếu platform không đảm bảo cache coherence:

```text
sync_for_device()
sync_for_cpu()
```

phải được backend thực hiện rõ ràng.

---

# 39. Raw pointer boundary

Raw pointer không được xem là I/O ownership token.

Không cho phép:

```text
device → arbitrary raw pointer
```

Thay vào đó:

```text
buffer_handle
region_handle
registered_buffer
```

Raw pointer chỉ được dùng sau khi memory contract đã được xác lập.

---

# 40. Cancellation

API:

```text
cancel(request_id)
cancel_all(context)
```

Semantics:

```text
CANCEL_REQUESTED
```

sau đó backend có thể:

```text
CANCELLED
```

hoặc operation có thể hoàn thành trước khi cancellation có hiệu lực.

---

# 41. Cancellation race

Race hợp lệ:

```text
submit
 │
 ├── cancel
 │
 └── completion
```

Có thể xảy ra:

```text
cancel requested
completion arrives
```

Runtime phải chọn **một terminal completion duy nhất**.

Không được:

```text
future.complete(CANCELLED)
future.complete(SUCCESS)
```

---

# 42. Deadline

Deadline luôn dùng:

```text
monotonic clock
```

không dùng wall-clock.

Ví dụ:

```text
deadline = now_monotonic() + 500ms
```

---

# 43. Deadline semantics

Có hai policy:

```text
CANCEL_ON_EXPIRY
```

hoặc:

```text
STOP_WAITING_ON_EXPIRY
```

Policy thứ hai nghĩa:

> caller ngừng chờ, nhưng I/O có thể vẫn đang chạy.

Đây là distinction bắt buộc.

---

# 44. Timer subsystem

Core:

```text
timer_source
```

hỗ trợ:

```text
one-shot
repeating
deadline
timeout
```

Ví dụ:

```text
await timer.sleep(100ms)
```

không tạo OS thread riêng.

---

# 45. Timer implementation

Backend được phép dùng:

```text
timerfd
kernel timers
IOCP timers
kqueue timers
host event loop
timer heap
timer wheel
```

Runtime lựa chọn dựa trên profile.

---

# 46. Timer coalescing

Các timer gần nhau có thể gom:

```text
1000.1 ms
1000.3 ms
1000.7 ms
```

thành một wakeup khoảng:

```text
1001 ms
```

nếu profile cho phép.

Realtime profile có thể cấm coalescing.

---

# 47. Event source

Generic:

```text
event_source
```

có thể đại diện:

```text
file readiness
socket readiness
completion port
device event
timer
IPC notification
host event
```

Mỗi source khai báo capability.

---

# 48. Device I/O

Core API:

```text
device_submit()
device_wait()
```

Device backend có thể sử dụng:

```text
DMA
interrupt
polling
completion queue
```

Device capability phải được kiểm tra qua `AXSECURITY`.

---

# 49. I/O context

`io_context` là execution environment cho I/O.

```text
io_context {
    backend
    completion_queue
    buffer_registry
    timer_registry
    limits
    tracing
    policy
}
```

Một process có thể có nhiều context.

---

# 50. Context isolation

Các context có thể có:

```text
separate completion queue
separate limits
separate buffer registry
separate trace session
```

Nhưng không tạo security authority mới.

---

# 51. Batch submission

API:

```text
submit_batch(operations[])
```

Backend có thể biến:

```text
64 submit()
```

thành:

```text
1 kernel submission
```

nếu hỗ trợ.

---

# 52. Batch completion

```text
drain_completions(64)
```

đọc nhiều completion một lần.

Đây là fast path quan trọng cho server/high-throughput runtime.

---

# 53. Queue capacity

Mỗi context có:

```text
max_inflight
max_queue_depth
max_buffer_bytes
```

Khi đầy:

```text
BLOCK
FAIL
THROTTLE
```

`DROP` chỉ hợp lệ với event stream nơi mất event được phép.

Không được silently drop:

```text
file write
database write
IPC command
```

---

# 54. Rate limiting

Có thể giới hạn:

```text
bytes/sec
operations/sec
concurrent operations
```

Nhưng đây là resource policy, không phải scheduler toàn hệ thống.

---

# 55. I/O priority

Operation có thể chứa:

```text
priority_hint
latency_class
background
interactive
deadline
```

Đây là **hint/contract**, không phải đảm bảo kernel phải ưu tiên tuyệt đối.

---

# 56. Reentrancy

# 87. Formal invariants

### ASYNC-INV-01
Mọi `io_operation` có một lifecycle state hợp lệ.

### ASYNC-INV-02
Mỗi terminal operation chỉ có một terminal completion.

### ASYNC-INV-03
`io_request_id` phải generation-safe.

### ASYNC-INV-04
Stale completion không được hoàn tất operation mới.

### ASYNC-INV-05
Cancellation request không đồng nghĩa cancellation completion.

### ASYNC-INV-06
Deadline dùng monotonic time.

### ASYNC-INV-07
Expiration không tự động imply kernel cancellation.

### ASYNC-INV-08
Partial I/O phải trả số byte thực tế.

### ASYNC-INV-09
Không được silently drop ordinary file writes.

### ASYNC-INV-10
Completion có thể xảy ra khác thread submit.

### ASYNC-INV-11
Không có global ordering mặc định giữa các request.

### ASYNC-INV-12
Ordering chỉ tồn tại khi semantic/backend contract cho phép.

### ASYNC-INV-13
Readiness event không được coi là completion.

### ASYNC-INV-14
Completion event không được yêu cầu caller thực hiện lại operation.

### ASYNC-INV-15
Async operation không được block AXTASK worker.

### ASYNC-INV-16
Sync bridge phải có blocking semantics rõ ràng.

### ASYNC-INV-17
Buffer đang IN_FLIGHT không được release.

### ASYNC-INV-18
Registered buffer phải còn valid trong toàn bộ operation.

### ASYNC-INV-19
Raw pointer không phải I/O ownership token.

### ASYNC-INV-20
DMA memory phải đáp ứng device visibility contract.

### ASYNC-INV-21
Cache coherency phải explicit khi platform yêu cầu.

### ASYNC-INV-22
Completion queue phải hỗ trợ batch drain.

### ASYNC-INV-23
Backend được phép tối ưu syscall batching.

### ASYNC-INV-24
Backend capability phải được khai báo trung thực.

### ASYNC-INV-25
Unsupported capability không được giả mạo là native capability.

### ASYNC-INV-26
I/O security authority không được tạo bởi AXASYNC.

### ASYNC-INV-27
Protected handle phải có authority hợp lệ từ AXSECURITY.

### ASYNC-INV-28
Process death invalidates process-owned in-flight I/O.

### ASYNC-INV-29
Peer death phải được biểu diễn bằng stable error.

### ASYNC-INV-30
Checkpoint không được giả định kernel I/O state có thể snapshot tùy ý.

### ASYNC-INV-31
Chỉ checkpointable/replay-safe intent mới được replay.

### ASYNC-INV-32
Simulation không được ảnh hưởng production backend ngoài explicit profile.

### ASYNC-INV-33
Fault injection phải explicit.

### ASYNC-INV-34
I/O trace mặc định không chứa payload.

### ASYNC-INV-35
Completion callback không được tạo recursive execution explosion.

### ASYNC-INV-36
Multiple submitter threads phải có semantics xác định.

### ASYNC-INV-37
Completion affinity chỉ là constraint khi operation yêu cầu.

### ASYNC-INV-38
I/O queue phải tôn trọng configured resource limits.

### ASYNC-INV-39
AXASYNC không sở hữu protocol semantics của AXNETWORK/AXIPC.

### ASYNC-INV-40
AXASYNC 5.0 phải giữ cùng semantic contract trên mọi backend; chỉ implementation/capability khác nhau.

# 9. Capability-based stream API

Ví dụ một network stream:

```text
readable
writable
duplex
async
```

nhưng có thể:

```text
not seekable
```

File stream:

```text
readable
writable
seekable
async
```

Compiler có thể reject:

```text

```

ngay ở compile time nếu type không có `seekable`.

# 10. Stream lifecycle

```text
CREATED
   │
   ▼
OPEN
   │
   ├────► HALF_CLOSED_READ
   │
   ├────► HALF_CLOSED_WRITE
   │
   ▼
CLOSING
   │
   ▼
CLOSED
```

Ngoài ra:

```text
FAILED
CANCELLED
```

# 11. EOF

EOF là trạng thái riêng.

Không được nhầm:

```text
read() == 0
```

với:

```text
temporary no data
```

Đối với finite stream:

```text
EOF
```

có nghĩa:

> sẽ không còn dữ liệu nữa.

# 12. Async stream

```text
async_stream
```

API:

```text
read_async()
write_async()
flush_async()
close_async()
```

Implementation dựa trên:

```text
AXASYNC
+
AXTASK
```

# 13. Async lowering

Axiom:

```text
let data = await stream.read_async(buf)
```

Compiler hạ:

```text
AXTASK state machine
        │
        ▼
AXSTREAM operation
        │
        ▼
AXASYNC submission
        │
        ▼
suspend
        │
        ▼
completion
        │
        ▼
resume
```

# 14. Không block async worker

Invariant:

```text
await stream.read_async()
```

không được biến thành:

```text
blocking read()
```

trên worker thread.

Nếu backend chỉ hỗ trợ blocking:

```text
blocking executor
```

phải được sử dụng explicit.

---

# 15. Read semantics

`read()` có thể trả:

```text
0..requested
```

bytes.

Không giả định full read.

Ví dụ:

```text
requested = 8192
actual = 2731
```

vẫn là thành công hợp lệ.

---

# 16. `read_exact`

```text
read_exact(buffer)
```

có semantic:

> tiếp tục đọc cho đến khi buffer đầy hoặc stream kết thúc/lỗi.

Nếu EOF trước khi đủ:

```text
UNEXPECTED_EOF
```

---

# 17. Write semantics

`write()` có thể ghi:

```text
0..requested
```

bytes.

`write_all()` đảm bảo:

```text
all requested bytes
```

hoặc trả lỗi.

Không silently discard phần còn lại.

---

# 18. Flush

`flush()` có nghĩa:

> đẩy dữ liệu đang được buffer ở tầng stream xuống tầng kế tiếp theo contract của stream.

Không mặc định có nghĩa:

> dữ liệu đã được physically persisted to storage.

Đối với persistence:

```text
AXSTORAGE
```

mới quyết định semantic tương ứng.

---

# 19. Close

`close()` phải idempotent.

```text
close()
close()
close()
```

không tạo double-free hoặc undefined behavior.

Sau `CLOSED`:

```text
read
write
flush
```

phải trả:

```text
STREAM_CLOSED
```

trừ các operation explicitly được phép sau close.

---

# 20. Duplex stream

Một stream có:

```text
read side
write side
```

độc lập.

Có thể:

```text
shutdown_write()
```

nhưng vẫn:

```text
read()
```

được.

---

# 21. Half-close

States:

```text
OPEN
 ├── READ_OPEN
 └── WRITE_OPEN
```

Sau:

```text
shutdown_write()
```

thì:

```text
WRITE_CLOSED
READ_OPEN
```

Điều này quan trọng cho TCP-like protocols.

# 22. Cursor

Stream seekable có:

```text
stream_cursor
```

gồm:

```text
position
origin
limits
```

API:

```text
tell()
seek()
skip()
rewind()
```

# 23. Seek origin

```text
BEGIN
CURRENT
END
```

Không cho phép `END` trên stream không có known finite length.

# 24. Random access

Seekable stream hỗ trợ:

```text
read_at(offset)
write_at(offset)
```

Các operation này không nhất thiết thay đổi shared cursor.

Đây là distinction quan trọng cho concurrent file access.

# 25. Concurrent cursor semantics

Hai task:

```text
task A → read()
task B → read()
```

trên cùng cursor phải có semantic được xác định.

Không để:

```text
A/B race → undefined cursor position
```

Options:

```text
serialized cursor
independent cursor
read_at/write_at
```

# 26. Buffering

Các mode:

```text
UNBUFFERED
BUFFERED
READ_AHEAD
WRITE_BEHIND
RING_BUFFER
```

Application có thể chọn profile.

# 27. Buffered read

```text
application
     │
     ▼
read()
     │
     ▼
stream buffer
     │
     ▼
underlying source
```

Nếu buffer còn dữ liệu:

```text
no underlying I/O
```

được phép.

---

# 28. Read-ahead

Runtime có thể đọc trước:

```text
requested = 4 KB
prefetch = 64 KB
```

nếu profile cho phép.

Không được vượt:

```text
memory budget
security limit
stream bounds
```

---

# 29. Write-behind

Application:

```text
write(A)
write(B)
write(C)
```

có thể tạo:

```text
buffer = A+B+C
```

rồi submit một operation lớn.

# 30. Ring buffer

High-throughput streams có thể dùng:

```text
ring_buffer
```

Ví dụ:

```text
producer
   ↓
┌─────────────────┐
│ ring buffer     │
└─────────────────┘
   ↓
consumer
```

Phù hợp:

- audio;
- video;
- network;
- telemetry;
- IPC;
- device streams.

# 31. Backpressure

Stream phải có flow control.

Nếu consumer chậm:

```text
producer
   ↓
buffer full
   ↓
BACKPRESSURE
```

Policy:

```text
BLOCK
ASYNC_WAIT
FAIL
THROTTLE
DROP
```

`DROP` chỉ hợp lệ nếu stream khai báo lossy semantics.

---

# 32. Không silently drop

Không được:

```text
write()
buffer full
→ silently discard
```

với:

- file;
- database;
- IPC command;
- ordinary network request.

---

# 33. Bounded stream

```text
bounded_stream(capacity)
```

phải có giới hạn rõ:

```text
max_bytes
max_messages
max_frames
```

Điều này đặc biệt quan trọng khi nhận dữ liệu không tin cậy.

# 34. Unbounded stream

Có thể hỗ trợ:

```text
unbounded_stream
```

nhưng runtime phải áp dụng:

```text
resource quota
```

Không có stream nào được phép tăng memory vô hạn ngoài policy.

# 35. Zero-copy

Stream có API:

```text
read_view()
peek()
consume()
```

Ví dụ:

```text
view = stream.peek()
```

trả:

```text
immutable byte span
```

không copy.

Sau:

```text
consume(n)
```

stream mới được phép tái sử dụng vùng buffer đó.

# 36. Ownership transfer

API có thể:

```text
read_owned_buffer()
```

và transfer ownership:

```text
stream → application
```

hoặc:

```text
application → stream
```

Không copy nếu backend hỗ trợ.

# 37. Buffer lifetime

View:

```text
stream_view
```

không được tồn tại sau khi underlying buffer bị recycle.

Compiler/debug runtime có thể kiểm tra lifetime trong mode phù hợp.

Production fast path không bắt buộc runtime tracking.

# 38. Framing

Byte stream vốn không có message boundary.

AXSTREAM cung cấp:

```text
frame
```

để biến:

```text
bytes...
```

thành:

```text
frame
frame
frame
```

Các framing strategy:

```text
FIXED_SIZE
DELIMITER
LENGTH_PREFIX
VARINT_LENGTH
CHUNKED
CUSTOM
```

---

# 39. Maximum frame size

Mọi frame decoder phải có:

```text
max_frame_size
```

Không được đọc:

```text
length = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
```

rồi allocate tương ứng.

---

# 40. Incremental framing

Decoder phải hỗ trợ partial input:

```text
input 1 → NEED_INPUT
input 2 → NEED_INPUT
input 3 → FRAME_READY
```

Không yêu cầu toàn bộ frame phải nằm trong một buffer.

---

# 41. Decoder state

Canonical state:

```text
NEED_INPUT
NEED_OUTPUT
PRODUCED
DONE
ERROR
```

Ví dụ:

```text
decode(input)
→ NEED_INPUT
```

là trạng thái bình thường, không phải error.

---

# 42. Delimiter framing

Ví dụ newline:

```text
frame1\n
frame2\n
frame3\n
```

Decoder phải hỗ trợ delimiter xuyên qua buffer boundary:

```text
buffer A: "hello"
buffer B: "\nworld"
```

vẫn tạo được:

```text
"hello"
```

---

# 43. Length-prefix framing

```text
[length][payload]
```

Length phải được validate trước khi allocation.

```text
if length > max_frame_size:
    FRAME_TOO_LARGE
```

---

# 44. Text line stream

API:

```text
read_line()
read_line_async()
write_line()
```

newline policy phải rõ:

```text
LF
CRLF
CR
ANY
```

Không silently thay đổi dữ liệu nếu mode raw.

# 45. UTF-8

UTF-8 là default.

Decoder phải xử lý:

- partial UTF-8 sequence;
- malformed sequence;
- overlong encoding;
- invalid scalar values.

Malformed policy:

```text
STRICT
REPLACE
PRESERVE_BYTES
```

# 46. Stateful decoding

Không giả định mỗi buffer là một text boundary.

Ví dụ một UTF-8 sequence có thể bị cắt:

```text
buffer A → first bytes
buffer B → remaining bytes
```

Decoder phải giữ state giữa các lần `decode()`.

# 47. Encoding separation

`AXSTREAM` cung cấp:

```text
text_stream
```

nhưng algorithm encoding/decoding phức tạp thuộc:

```text
AXCODEC
```

AXSTREAM chỉ compose chúng.

# 48. Stream filters

Một stream có thể tạo pipeline:

```text
source
  ↓
buffer
  ↓
decoder
  ↓
transform
  ↓
consumer
```

```text
 ↓
decompression
 ↓
UTF-8 decoder

line reader
```

# 49. Pipeline

Core:

```text
stream_pipeline
```

Ví dụ:

```text
  → decompress
```

```text
input
output

limits
flush
```

Nếu stage nhận ownership:

# 51. Compression boundary

Compression là filter:

```text
  ↓
```

# 52. Checksum boundary

```text
 ↓
```

```text
 ▼   ▼
A    B
```

Hỗ trợ:

# 89. Formal invariants

### STREAM-INV-01
Mỗi stream có lifecycle state hợp lệ.

### STREAM-INV-02
Closed stream không nhận ordinary I/O.

### STREAM-INV-03
`close()` idempotent.

### STREAM-INV-04
EOF khác temporary no-data.

### STREAM-INV-05
Partial read phải trả số byte thực tế.

### STREAM-INV-06
Partial write phải trả số byte thực tế.

### STREAM-INV-07
`read_exact()` không được coi partial success là complete.

### STREAM-INV-08
`write_all()` không được silently discard bytes.

### STREAM-INV-09
Flush không mặc định đồng nghĩa physical persistence.

### STREAM-INV-10
Seek chỉ tồn tại trên seekable stream.

### STREAM-INV-11
`read_at/write_at` không tự động thay đổi shared cursor.

### STREAM-INV-12
Concurrent cursor access phải có semantic xác định.

### STREAM-INV-13
Async stream operation không block async worker.

### STREAM-INV-14
Stream view không được tồn tại ngoài lifetime contract của backing buffer.

### STREAM-INV-15
Buffer ownership transfer phải explicit.

### STREAM-INV-16
Stream không được release buffer đang in-flight.

### STREAM-INV-17
Backpressure phải observable.

### STREAM-INV-18
Bounded stream không vượt configured capacity.

### STREAM-INV-19
Lossy stream phải explicit.

### STREAM-INV-20
Ordinary file/network/IPC data không được silently drop.

### STREAM-INV-21
Frame decoder phải có maximum frame size.

### STREAM-INV-22
Partial frame phải được hỗ trợ.

### STREAM-INV-23
Malformed frame không được biến thành EOF.

### STREAM-INV-24
Text decoder phải xử lý sequence xuyên buffer boundary.

### STREAM-INV-25
UTF-8 là default text encoding.

### STREAM-INV-26
Malformed text policy phải explicit.

### STREAM-INV-27
Filter pipeline phải giữ ownership semantics.

### STREAM-INV-28
Pipeline error phải propagate theo policy.

### STREAM-INV-29
Compression không thuộc byte-stream semantic core.

### STREAM-INV-30
IPC message ABI không thuộc AXSTREAM.

### STREAM-INV-31
Network protocol không thuộc AXSTREAM.

### STREAM-INV-32
Filesystem semantics không thuộc AXSTREAM.

### STREAM-INV-33
Security authority không được tạo bởi stream.

### STREAM-INV-34
Cancellation khác timeout.

### STREAM-INV-35
Deadline dùng monotonic clock.

### STREAM-INV-36
Trace mặc định không capture payload.

### STREAM-INV-37
Fault injection chỉ active dưới explicit diagnostic/test profile.

### STREAM-INV-38
Simulation không thay đổi production semantics.

### STREAM-INV-39
Stream abstraction không bắt buộc heap allocation trên hot path.

### STREAM-INV-40
AXSTREAM 5.0 phải duy trì semantic contract độc lập với backend.

# BOOTSTRAP-751 — AXCODEC

**Native Encoding, Serialization, Compression, Checksum & Framing Codec Runtime**

Mục tiêu tiếp theo là xây `AXCODEC` thành tầng codec độc lập với `AXSTREAM`: compiler-generated serialization, UTF/text codecs, binary layouts, schema/version evolution, deterministic/canonical encoding, compression, checksums, incremental encode/decode, bounded untrusted-input decoding, zero-copy decode và codec pipelines.

`AXCODEC` sẽ là lớp giúp Axiom có thể biến trực tiếp:

```text
Axiom Type
    ↓
Generated Codec
    ↓
bytes
    ↓
AXSTREAM / AXIPC / AXSTORAGE / AXNETWORK
```

mà **không cần reflection runtime và không cần third-party serialization runtime**.
