# 21. Stop Semantics

Every stop must have a reason.

```text
StopReason {
    kind
    thread
    address?
    breakpoint_id?
    signal?
    exception?
    trap?
    watchpoint?
    step?
}
```

Kinds:

```text
BREAKPOINT
WATCHPOINT
STEP
PAUSE
SIGNAL
EXCEPTION
PANIC
TRAP
FAULT
ENTRY
MODULE_EVENT
TASK_EVENT
USER_INTERRUPT
```

The debugger must never infer:

```text
"probably breakpoint"
```

when the backend supplied a precise reason.

---

# 22. Continue Semantics

`continue` resumes the target from the current stop point.

If stopped because of a software breakpoint, the debugger performs the required platform-specific breakpoint-step-over procedure before continuing.

This must be invisible to the user but explicit in the backend state machine.

---

# 23. Software Breakpoints

Software breakpoint:

```text
SoftwareBreakpoint {
    id
    address
    original_bytes
    trap_encoding
    module
    verified
}
```

The original instruction bytes must be retained.

Never restore bytes belonging to a newer image or changed module.

---

# 24. Breakpoint Identity

Stable identity:

```text
BreakpointIdentity {
    symbol_id?
    source_file_id?
    source_range?
    module_identity?
    logical_key
}
```

Address alone is not a stable identity.

Recompilation can change addresses while preserving:

```text
SymbolId
source location
module identity
```

---

# 25. Hardware Breakpoints

Hardware breakpoints are architecture-specific.

They must expose:

```text
slot_count
instruction_slots
data_slots
supported_sizes
supported_access_modes
```

If slots are exhausted:

```text
DEBUG_HARDWARE_SLOTS_EXHAUSTED
```

must be returned.

No automatic silent conversion to software breakpoints when semantics differ.

---

# 26. Conditional Breakpoints

```text
ConditionalBreakpoint {
    breakpoint
    condition
    evaluation_policy
}
```

Default evaluation:

```text
READ_ONLY
NO_SIDE_EFFECT
```

Condition failures must not modify application state.

---

# 27. Hit-Count Breakpoints

```text
HitPolicy {
    break_on_count
    break_every
    break_after
}
```

Counters belong to debugger session state unless explicitly persisted.

---

# 28. Logpoints

A logpoint executes debugger-side formatting based on captured state.

It must not silently inject application code.

```text
Logpoint {
    breakpoint
    template
    expressions[]
}
```

Expressions follow the same side-effect policy as watch expressions.

---

# 29. Watchpoints

```text
Watchpoint {
    id
    address
    size
    access
    hardware
    condition?
}
```

Access:

```text
READ
WRITE
READ_WRITE
```

Watchpoints are inherently limited by hardware.

The debugger must report:

```text
EXACT
PARTIAL
UNSUPPORTED
```

semantics.

---

# 30. Exception / Panic / Trap Breakpoints

Debugger configuration:

```text
break_on_exception
break_on_panic
break_on_trap
break_on_signal
break_on_fault
```

Axiom panic/trap metadata should identify:

```text
panic code
source location
message reference
originating function
stack
```

without requiring the production runtime to contain a large debugger.

---

# 31. Function Breakpoints

Function breakpoint:

```text
FunctionBreakpoint {
    symbol
    module?
    overload_identity?
}
```

When the module is not loaded:

```text
PENDING
```

The debugger resolves it after `ModuleLoaded`.

---

# 32. Pending Breakpoints

States:

```text
PENDING
RESOLVED
VERIFIED
INVALID
DISABLED
```

A pending breakpoint is not an error.

---

# 33. Breakpoint Verification

Every resolved breakpoint records:

```text
requested_location
resolved_address
module_identity
verification_state
```

Verification may compare:

- instruction bytes;
- symbol identity;
- source mapping;
- module build ID.

---

# 34. Register Model

Canonical:

```text
RegisterSet {
    general[]
    flags?
    control?
    vector[]
    special[]
}
```

Each register:

```text
Register {
    id
    name
    width
    category
    value
    writable
}
```

---

# 35. x86-64 Registers

Baseline:

```text
RAX RBX RCX RDX
RSI RDI RBP RSP
R8-R15
RIP
RFLAGS
```

Debug information may additionally expose:

```text
XMM
YMM
ZMM
MXCSR
segment registers
debug registers
```

depending on backend capability.

---

# 36. AArch64 Registers

Baseline:

```text
X0-X30
SP
PC
PSTATE
```

Vector:

```text
V0-V31
```

with appropriate SIMD/FP interpretation.

---

# 37. Vector Register Model

Vector values must not be forced into scalar representations.

```text
VectorRegister {
    width
    bytes
    lanes?
    lane_type?
}
```

The UI can provide multiple interpretations without changing stored register state.

---

# 38. Register Read/Write

```text
debug_read_register()
debug_write_register()
debug_read_register_set()
debug_write_register_set()
```

Writes require:

```text
target stopped
register writable
architecture-compatible value
```

A failed write must not partially corrupt a register set.

---

# 39. Memory Model

```text
DebugMemory {
    address
    size
    permissions
    region
    bytes
}
```

Permissions:

```text
READ
WRITE
EXECUTE
GUARD
SHARED
PRIVATE
```

---

# 40. Memory Regions

```text
MemoryRegion {
    base
    size
    permissions
    mapped
    module?
    name?
}
```

Examples:

```text
CODE
RODATA
DATA
HEAP
STACK
TLS
SHARED_LIBRARY
MMIO
GUARD
UNKNOWN
```

---

# 41. Memory Read

Reads must return partial results safely.

```text
MemoryReadResult {
    bytes
    valid_prefix
    fault_address?
}
```

A page boundary must not cause the debugger to fabricate bytes.

---

# 42. Memory Write

Memory writes require:

```text
explicit debugger operation
target stopped
writable region or explicit override
```

Debugger UI inspection must never accidentally turn into a write.

---

# 43. Stack Model

```text
StackInfo {
    thread
    current_sp
    stack_base
    stack_limit
    growth_direction
}
```

Stack memory may contain:

- return addresses;
- locals;
- saved registers;
- arguments;
- task frames;
- runtime frames.

---

# 44. Stack Unwinding

Preferred order:

```text
1. precise debug/unwind metadata
2. platform unwind metadata
3. frame-pointer chain
4. architecture fallback
5. stop with UNKNOWN
```

The debugger must never fabricate a frame.

---

# 45. Frame Model

```text
DebugFrame {
    index
    instruction_address
    function
    module
    source
    inline_chain[]
    registers?
    locals
    arguments
}
```

---

# 46. Inline Frames

An optimized function may contain multiple logical source frames at one machine-code address.

Therefore:

```text
physical frame
    ↓
inline chain
    ↓
logical source frames
```

must be represented explicitly.

---

# 47. Source Mapping

Canonical mapping:

```text
InstructionAddress
      ↕
SourceLocation
```

```text
SourceLocation {
    file_id
    line
    column
    end_line?
    end_column?
}
```

Mapping must include:

```text
statement boundaries
expression locations
inline locations
function ranges
```

---

# 48. Source Identity

Paths are not sufficient.

Use:

```text
SourceFileIdentity {
    content_hash?
    canonical_path?
    source_id
}
```

This allows source mapping after source trees move.

---

# 49. Source Remapping

Debug session may specify:

```text
SourceMap {
    compiled_root
    local_root
    remote_root?
}
```

Mappings are deterministic and ordered.

---

# 50. Variable Model

```text
DebugVariable {
    name
    type
    location
    value_state
    children[]
    scope
    flags
}
```

Value states:

```text
AVAILABLE
OPTIMIZED_OUT
UNAVAILABLE
UNREADABLE
NOT_IN_SCOPE
UNKNOWN
```

---

# 51. No Fabricated Values

If the compiler reports a variable as optimized out:

```text
OPTIMIZED_OUT
```

must be displayed.

The debugger must never invent a plausible value from nearby registers or memory.

---

# 52. Local Variables

Scopes:

```text
GLOBAL
MODULE
FUNCTION
BLOCK
LOOP
TASK
CLOSURE
```

Scope validity follows compiler metadata.

---

# 53. Global Variables

Globals require:

```text
module identity
symbol identity
storage address
type metadata
```

ASLR must not invalidate symbolic identity.

---

# 54. Static Variables

Static storage must distinguish:

```text
module static
function static
thread-local static
process global
```

---

# 55. Aggregate Values

Axiom structs:

```text
StructValue {
    type_id
    fields[]
}
```

Enums:

```text
EnumValue {
    type_id
    discriminant
    variant
    payload?
}
```

Unions:

```text
UnionValue {
    type_id
    active_variant?
    raw_storage
}
```

---

# 56. Pointer Values

```text
PointerValue {
    address
    pointee_type?
    nullable
}
```

The debugger must distinguish:

```text
null
valid mapped address
unmapped address
non-readable address
unknown provenance
```

---

# 57. Slice Values

Axiom slices are decoded according to AXABI.

Conceptually:

```text
Slice<T> {
    ptr
    len
}
```

The debugger must know the exact compiler-emitted representation rather than assume it.

---

# 58. String Values

Axiom `String` and `Str` are decoded using compiler ABI metadata.

The debugger should provide:

```text
raw bytes
UTF-8 interpretation
length
capacity where applicable
```

without reading beyond validated bounds.

---

# 59. C ABI Values

Foreign values use:

```text
extern "C"
```

ABI metadata.

AXDEBUGGER supports:

- C integer types;
- floating-point types;
- pointers;
- structs;
- arrays;
- enums;
- ABI-defined aggregates.

---

# 60. Native Axiom Types

Every debug-capable compiled type may have:

```text
TypeDebugDescriptor {
    type_id
    name
    kind
    size
    alignment
    fields[]
    variants[]
    generic_args[]
    layout
}
```

---

# 61. Generic Types

Generics are normally monomorphized.

Therefore the debugger sees:

```text
Vector<i32>
Vector<f64>
Vector<MyStruct>
```

as concrete instantiated types where available.

---

# 62. Generic Symbol Identity

A generic instantiation identity includes:

```text
generic_definition_id
type_arguments[]
module_identity
```

This avoids ambiguity between different monomorphizations.

---

# 63. Closure Values

Closures are represented according to compiler-generated debug metadata.

Conceptually:

```text
ClosureValue {
    function
    environment
}
```

Captured variables are exposed when their storage is available.

---

# 64. Function Values

```text
FunctionValue {
    code_address
    function_type
    environment?
}
```

The debugger distinguishes:

```text
plain function pointer
closure
method value
foreign function pointer
```

---

# 65. Expression Evaluation

Architecture:

```text
AXIDE expression
       ↓
AXDEBUGGER
       ↓
compiler semantic/type service
       ↓
debug evaluator
       ↓
target state
```

Expressions must reuse Axiom's semantic rules.

The debugger must not implement a second incompatible Axiom language parser.

---

# 66. Expression Modes

```text
READ_ONLY
DEBUG_MUTATING
RAW_MACHINE
```

Default:

```text READ_ONLY
```

---

# 67. Read-Only Evaluation

Read-only evaluation may:

- inspect locals;
- inspect fields;
- perform arithmetic;
- perform comparisons;
- dereference readable memory;
- call pure debugger-provided formatting operations.

It must not mutate target state.

---

# 68. Mutating Evaluation

Mutation requires explicit user action.

Examples:

```text
set variable
set memory
set register
```

are distinct debugger operations.

They must not be hidden inside an ordinary watch expression.

---

# 69. Function Calls From Debugger

Calling target functions is dangerous because it can:

- mutate state;
- allocate;
- block;
- acquire locks;
- trigger I/O;
- deadlock.

Therefore target function calls are disabled by default.

If supported:

```text
EXPLICIT_DEBUG_CALL
```

must be a distinct operation with clear side-effect semantics and cancellation limitations.

---

# 70. Compiler/Debugger Expression Bridge

Canonical interface:

```text
debug_parse_expression()
debug_typecheck_expression()
debug_lower_expression()
debug_evaluate_expression()
```

The compiler supplies:

```text
types
operators
casts
names
generic rules
member lookup
```

The debugger supplies:

```text
runtime values
memory
registers
frame context
```

---

# 71. Async/Task Debugging

Axiom task:

```text
Task {
    id
    state
    continuation
    stack_state
    executor
    current_thread?
}
```

A task may be:

```text
READY
RUNNING
WAITING
SUSPENDED
COMPLETED
FAILED
CANCELLED
```

---

# 72. Task Stack

An async task may not have a conventional contiguous OS-thread stack.

Debugger therefore needs:

```text
logical task frame
↓
suspended state
↓
compiler-generated continuation state
```

---

# 73. Coroutine State

Compiler emits task debug metadata describing:

```text
state machine
state identifier
suspended variables
resume function
await location
```

This permits source-level debugging across `await`.

---

# 74. Task-to-Thread Mapping

When running:

```text
Task A → Thread 3
```

After rescheduling:

```text
Task A → Thread 7
```

the debugger preserves Task A's logical identity.

---

# 75. Concurrency Inspection

Debugger exposes:

```text
threads
tasks
executors
locks
waits
channels
condition variables
```

where metadata is available.

---

# 76. Synchronization State

Canonical:

```text
SyncWait {
    waiter
    resource
    owner?
    state
}
```

The debugger may construct a wait graph:

```text
Thread A
   ↓ waits
Lock X
   ↓ owned by
Thread B
```

---

# 77. Deadlock Inspection

AXDEBUGGER may report suspected cycles:

```text
A → B → C → A
```

but this is an inspection result, not a guarantee of a deadlock unless the runtime/platform provides sufficient evidence.

---

# 78. Race Diagnostics Boundary

Race detection belongs to a dedicated subsystem/tooling layer.

AXDEBUGGER may consume:

```text
race event
race report
instrumentation metadata
```

but does not become the race detector.

---

# 79. Source-Level Stepping

`step_into` follows the next source-level executable location.

Compiler metadata must identify:

```text
statement
expression
call boundary
inline boundary
```

---

# 80. Step Over

`step_over` executes the current source operation without entering called functions where possible.

For optimized/inlined code, exact semantics depend on available debug metadata.

---

# 81. Step Out

`step_out` resumes until the current logical frame exits.

Inline frames require special treatment because an inline frame may not correspond to an independent machine stack frame.

---

# 82. Instruction Stepping

```text
step_instruction()
```

operates on machine instructions.

It is always available only where the platform backend supports it.

---

# 83. Run to Cursor

The IDE may request:

```text
run_to_source_location()
```

AXDEBUGGER resolves the source location and uses a temporary breakpoint.

The temporary breakpoint is removed after the stop.

---

# 84. Reverse Debugging Boundary

Reverse execution is **optional**.

AXDEBUGGER defines the interface:

```text
reverse_continue()
reverse_step()
checkpoint()
restore_checkpoint()
```

but does not require a general reverse-execution engine in v5.0.

If unavailable:

```text
DEBUG_REVERSE_UNSUPPORTED
```

---

# 85. Deterministic Replay

AXDEBUGGER can integrate with deterministic replay infrastructure.

Required metadata:

```text
replay_session_id
event_sequence
checkpoint_id
execution_generation
```

Replay itself belongs to a dedicated runtime/debug infrastructure layer.

---

# 86. Watch / Inspect Contract

AXCODEEDITOR and AXGUI must never directly access target memory.

They call:

```text
AXDEBUGGER
```

through an immutable inspection result.

```text
InspectionSnapshot {
    session_generation
    stop_generation
    variables[]
    frames[]
    memory_views[]
}
```

---

# 87. AXCODEEDITOR Integration

AXCODEEDITOR displays:

```text
breakpoint markers
current instruction
execution line
inline variable hints
diagnostic state
```

AXDEBUGGER owns all semantic state.

---

# 88. Breakpoint UI Contract

```text
BreakpointPresentation {
    breakpoint_id
    source_location
    enabled
    verified
    pending
    condition
    hit_count
}
```

AXCODEEDITOR never directly installs machine breakpoints.

---

# 300. Fundamental Invariants

The following invariants are normative.

### DEBUG-INV-01
A debugger session must have a unique session identity.

### DEBUG-INV-02
Every target control operation belongs to exactly one session.

### DEBUG-INV-03
AXDEBUGGER must distinguish process, OS thread, Axiom task and async continuation.

### DEBUG-INV-04
Target mutation is serialized.

### DEBUG-INV-05
Read-only inspection may execute concurrently where backend-safe.

### DEBUG-INV-06
Every asynchronous result carries generation information.

### DEBUG-INV-07
Stale results must not mutate current debugger state.

### DEBUG-INV-08
A breakpoint address is not its canonical identity.

### DEBUG-INV-09
Persistent breakpoints use symbolic/source identity where available.

### DEBUG-INV-10
Software breakpoint restoration must verify expected trap bytes.

### DEBUG-INV-11
Hardware breakpoint limitations must be reported explicitly.

### DEBUG-INV-12
Unsupported watchpoint semantics must not be simulated deceptively.

### DEBUG-INV-13
Register reads must respect backend architecture.

### DEBUG-INV-14
Register writes require an explicitly stopped target.

### DEBUG-INV-15
Memory reads must be bounds-checked.

### DEBUG-INV-16
Memory writes require explicit authorization.

### DEBUG-INV-17
Unmapped memory must never be represented as valid data.

### DEBUG-INV-18
Stack unwinding must never fabricate frames.

### DEBUG-INV-19
Inline frames must be distinguishable from physical frames.

### DEBUG-INV-20
Optimized-out variables must remain explicitly optimized-out.

### DEBUG-INV-21
Variable decoding must use ABI/type metadata when available.

### DEBUG-INV-22
Generic values must preserve concrete type arguments.

### DEBUG-INV-23
Async tasks must not be modeled as OS threads.

### DEBUG-INV-24
Task migration must preserve logical task identity.

### DEBUG-INV-25
Expression evaluation is read-only by default.

### DEBUG-INV-26
Target function calls are never implicit.

### DEBUG-INV-27
Expression evaluation must obey resource limits.

### DEBUG-INV-28
AXDEBUGGER must not become the profiling subsystem.

### DEBUG-INV-29
Release builds must not contain mandatory debugger runtime overhead.

### DEBUG-INV-30
Debug artifacts must be independently identifiable from binaries.

### DEBUG-INV-31
Mismatched debug artifacts must be rejected by default.

### DEBUG-INV-32
Remote debugging must authenticate before privileged operations.

### DEBUG-INV-33
Remote debugging must not be enabled publicly by default.

### DEBUG-INV-34
Postmortem sessions must not mutate target state.

### DEBUG-INV-35
Corrupt target state must not corrupt debugger state.

### DEBUG-INV-36
Debug metadata parsing must enforce resource limits.

### DEBUG-INV-37
AXIDE/AXCODEEDITOR must not directly control target memory or execution.

### DEBUG-INV-38
Compiler semantic metadata is authoritative over debugger heuristics.

### DEBUG-INV-39
AXDEBUGGER ABI changes require explicit ABI versioning.

### DEBUG-INV-40
Every conforming AXDEBUGGER implementation must satisfy all mandatory invariants above.

# 1. Purpose

AXPROFILER is the native Axiom performance-analysis subsystem.

Its purpose is to answer:

```text
Where is execution time spent?
Why is it spent there?
Which functions consume CPU?
Which tasks wait?
Where are allocations occurring?
Which locks cause contention?
How does execution evolve over time?
Which code paths scale poorly?
```

Architecture:

```text
                         APPLICATION
                              │
              ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
              │               │               │
          CPU execution    Memory          Tasks/Async
              │               │               │
              ▼               ▼               ▼
         AXPROFILER     AXMEMORY/Runtime    AXTASK
              │               │               │
              └───────────────┼───────────────┘
                              ▼
                       PROFILE ENGINE
                              │
                ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
                │             │             │
             Samples      Events        Counters
                │             │             │
                └─────────────┼─────────────┘
                              ▼
                       Aggregation Engine
                              │
                 ┌────────────┼────────────┐
                 │            │            │
             Call Tree     Timeline    Statistics
                 │            │            │
                 └────────────┼────────────┘
                              ▼
                        Profile Artifact
                              │
                    AXIDE / AXGUI / AI
```

---

# 2. Fundamental Boundary

AXDEBUGGER answers:

> **What is the target doing at this exact stopped moment?**

AXPROFILER answers:

> **What did the target spend time/resources doing over an interval?**

Therefore:

```text
AXDEBUGGER = state inspection
AXPROFILER = statistical/performance analysis
```

Neither subsystem replaces the other.

---

# 3. Non-Goals

AXPROFILER does not own:

- debugger breakpoints;
- source editing;
- general logging;
- production telemetry;
- crash reporting;
- executable loading;
- compiler optimization;
- memory allocation itself;
- scheduler implementation;
- hardware performance-counter configuration outside profiling.

---

Axiom defines:

```text
PROFILE_COUNTER
PROFILE_MEMORY
PROFILE_CONCURRENCY
PROFILE_TASK
PROFILE_TIMELINE
PROFILE_TRACE
PROFILE_COMBINED
```

The application chooses explicitly.

# 5. Default Philosophy

The default profiler must be:

```text

sampling-first
opt-in
bounded
deterministic in artifact structure
platform-aware
```

Instrumentation is available when sampling cannot answer the required question.

# 11. Sampling Profiler

Sampling is the primary low-overhead profiler.

Concept:

```text
timer/hardware interrupt
        ↓
capture execution state
        ↓
instruction pointer
        ↓
stack
        ↓
symbol/source mapping
        ↓
sample
```

No application instrumentation is required.

# 12. Sample Model

```text
ProfileSample {
    timestamp
    process_id
    thread_id
    task_id?
    cpu_id?
    instruction_pointer
    stack[]
    state
}
```

# 13. Sampling Frequency

Configuration may specify:

```text
samples_per_second
```

Typical modes:

```text LOW
MEDIUM
HIGH
CUSTOM
```

The profiler must prevent unsafe frequencies that exceed backend/platform capabilities.

---

# 14. Sampling Overhead

Sampling must be designed around:

```text short interrupt path
minimal allocation
per-thread buffers
deferred symbolization
```

The hot path should not:

```text allocate
lock globally
perform symbol lookup
format strings
write files synchronously
```

---

# 15. Per-Thread Buffers

Each profiling thread receives:

```text
lock-free or low-contention ring buffer
```

Concept:

```text Thread
  ↓
Local SampleBuffer
  ↓
background drain
  ↓
aggregator
```

---

# 16. Buffer Overflow

If the buffer fills:

```text samples_dropped++
```

must be recorded.

The profiler must never pretend that dropped samples exist.

---

# 17. Sample Quality

Every sample has:

```text validity
capture_quality
stack_quality
symbolization_quality
```

Possible states:

```text COMPLETE
PARTIAL_STACK
UNKNOWN_SYMBOL
STACK_UNAVAILABLE
DROPPED
```

---

# 18. Stack Sampling

Preferred:

```text unwind metadata
```

Fallback:

```text frame pointers
```

Then:

```text architecture fallback
```

The profiler must never fabricate stack frames.

---

# 19. Stack Depth

Configurable:

```text max_stack_depth
```

A bounded default prevents pathological recursive stacks from exhausting buffers.

---

# 20. Call Tree

Samples are aggregated into:

```text CallTree
```

Example:

```text main
 ├── render
 │    ├── layout
 │    └── raster
 └── update
      ├── physics
      └── input
```

```text
ProfileCallNode {

    inclusive_time?
    exclusive_time?
    children[]
}
```

# 22. Inclusive Cost

A function's inclusive cost includes:

```text function itself
+
all descendant execution
```

---

# 23. Exclusive Cost

Exclusive cost measures execution attributed directly to the function.

For sampling:

```text exclusive sample
```

means the sampled stack's leaf frame is the function.

Sampling results are estimates.


# 293. Final Design Decisions

AXPROFILER 5.0 permanently establishes:

1. **Sampling is the primary low-overhead profiler.**
2. **Instrumentation is explicitly opt-in.**
3. **Release binaries have no mandatory profiling runtime.**
4. **CPU, wall and wait time are distinct metrics.**
5. **Axiom tasks are distinct from OS threads.**
6. **Hardware counters are capability-driven.**
7. **Allocation profiling does not capture memory contents by default.**
8. **Raw collection is separated from expensive symbolization.**
9. **Large profiles use streaming/chunked storage.**
10. **`.axprof` is the canonical profile artifact.**
11. **PGO export is a defined compiler boundary.**
12. **AXPROFILER does not make optimization decisions itself.**
13. **AXDEBUGGER remains responsible for interactive target inspection.**
14. **AXOBSERVABILITY remains responsible for general telemetry.**
15. **AXCRASH remains responsible for crash reporting.**
16. **Remote profiling is authenticated and capability-controlled.**
17. **Every statistical result retains measurement provenance.**
18. **Dropped/partial/unresolved data is explicitly represented.**
19. **Profile aggregation is deterministic for identical captured data.**
20. **The profiler is designed around bounded overhead and bounded memory.**

# 1. Purpose

AXCRASH is the native Axiom subsystem responsible for capturing and preserving abnormal process termination and execution-fault state.

Its fundamental question is:

> **What happened when the program failed, and what evidence can be preserved for later analysis?**

Architecture:

```text
                         Axiom Application
                                │
              ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐
              │                 │                 │
           Panic/Trap       OS Exception       Fatal Fault
              │                 │                 │
              └─────────────────┼─────────────────┘
                                ▼
                           AXCRASH
                                │
               ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
               │                │                │
          Fault Capture    State Capture    Artifact Writer
               │                │                │
               └────────────────┼────────────────┘
                                ▼
                         .axcrash artifact
                                │
              ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐
              │                 │                 │
         Local Analysis    AXIDE/Debugger    Remote Collection
              │                 │                 │
              └─────────────────┼─────────────────┘
                                ▼
                         Postmortem Analysis
```

---

# 2. Fundamental Boundary

The architectural distinction is:

```text
AXDEBUGGER  = interactive live execution inspection
AXPROFILER  = performance measurement
AXDIAGNOSTICS = general diagnostic information
AXOBSERVABILITY = telemetry
AXCRASH     = abnormal termination evidence
```

AXCRASH must remain independent of the debugger.

A production application can therefore generate a crash artifact without containing the full debugger.

---

# 3. Non-Goals

AXCRASH does not own:

- compiler optimization;
- debugger breakpoints;
- profiling;
- ordinary logging;
- application telemetry;
- OS process creation;
- executable loading;
- exception policy;
- security authorization;
- source editing;
- automatic source modification.

---

# 4. Crash Definition

A crash is an abnormal execution termination that requires diagnostic preservation.

Examples:

```text
invalid memory access
illegal instruction
divide/trap fault
stack exhaustion
explicit fatal panic
uncaught fatal runtime error
OS exception
fatal signal
abort
runtime invariant violation
```

Exact classification is platform-dependent.

---

```text

   │
   ▼
FAULT_DETECTED
   │
   ▼
CAPTURE
   │
   ├── capture failed ──► MINIMAL_CAPTURE
   │
   ▼
FINALIZE
   │
   ▼
ARTIFACT_READY
   │
   ├── local persistence
   └── optional remote submission
```

# 42. Handler Constraints

Crash-time code must assume:

```text heap may be corrupted
locks may be held
allocator may be broken
other threads may be inconsistent
runtime state may be partially destroyed
```

Therefore crash handling requires a restricted emergency path.

# 43. Emergency Allocator

AXCRASH may reserve a small emergency memory region at startup:


# 45. No Normal Allocator Dependency

The emergency crash path must not depend on the normal allocator being functional.

---

# 46. Crash-Time Lock Avoidance

Crash capture must avoid global locks where possible.

A deadlocked process cannot depend on the deadlocked lock to produce its crash artifact.

---

# 47. Crash Serialization

The emergency path writes:

```text bounded binary records
```

rather than constructing large object graphs.

# 1. Purpose

AXREPLAY provides deterministic recording and replay of Axiom program execution.

Its central goal is:

```text
execution
    ↓
record nondeterministic decisions
    ↓
replay same decisions
    ↓
reproduce equivalent execution
```

The primary use cases are:

- deterministic debugging;
- reproducing intermittent crashes;
- reverse debugging foundation;
- concurrency debugging;
- async/task debugging;
- regression reproduction;
- deterministic test failure reproduction;
- crash-to-replay workflows;
- diagnosing race-sensitive behavior;
- performance investigation with reproducible execution context.

---

# 2. Fundamental Principle

AXREPLAY does **not** record every CPU instruction by default.

Instead it records the minimum externally observable nondeterministic information necessary to reproduce execution under a defined replay contract.

```text
                    Program
                       │
             ┌─────────┴─────────┐
             │                   │
       Deterministic        Nondeterministic
          state                   events
             │                   │
             │              AXREPLAY Recorder
             │                   │
             └─────────┬─────────┘
                       ▼
                  .axreplay
                       │
                       ▼
                 Replay Engine
                       │
                       ▼
              Equivalent execution
```

This keeps recording substantially cheaper than instruction-by-instruction tracing.

---

# 3. Scope Boundary

```text
AXREPLAY = execution determinism
AXCRASH  = crash evidence
AXDEBUGGER = interactive inspection
AXPROFILER = performance measurement
AXTEST = verification
```

AXREPLAY may integrate all of them but does not replace them.

---

# 4. Non-Goals

AXREPLAY does not guarantee:

- identical wall-clock timing;
- identical physical CPU execution;
- identical cache behavior;
- identical hardware-counter values;
- identical OS scheduling outside the replay contract;
- reproduction of arbitrary external systems not captured by the recorder.

---


# 252. Concurrency Collections

---

# 255. Timeout Races

When a timeout races with another event, replay records the selected winner.

# 256. Scheduler Fairness

# 281. Replay Security Invariants

### REPLAY-INV-01
Every replay artifact has a unique session identity.

### REPLAY-INV-02
Every artifact identifies the exact target contract.

### REPLAY-INV-03
Every required nondeterministic event has an ordered sequence.

### REPLAY-INV-04
Required events cannot be silently dropped.

### REPLAY-INV-05
Optional dropped events are explicitly recorded.

### REPLAY-INV-06
Strict replay stops on required divergence.

### REPLAY-INV-07
Strict replay never silently falls back to nondeterministic execution.

### REPLAY-INV-08
Replay validates executable build identity.

### REPLAY-INV-09
Replay validates runtime compatibility.

### REPLAY-INV-10
Replay validates module identities.

### REPLAY-INV-11
Logical task identity remains distinct from OS thread identity.

### REPLAY-INV-12
Scheduler replay preserves recorded logical scheduling decisions.

### REPLAY-INV-13
Time virtualization preserves recorded values where required.

### REPLAY-INV-14
Randomness required for determinism is reproduced exactly.

### REPLAY-INV-15
External input required for determinism is reproduced exactly.

### REPLAY-INV-16
Network replay does not automatically contact recorded endpoints.

### REPLAY-INV-17
Filesystem replay does not automatically mutate the real filesystem.

### REPLAY-INV-18
Child-process replay is explicitly controlled.

### REPLAY-INV-19
Replay artifacts cannot execute embedded code.

### REPLAY-INV-20
Replay artifacts enforce resource limits.

### REPLAY-INV-21
Replay memory capture is not enabled implicitly without policy.

### REPLAY-INV-22
Replay checkpoints are immutable.

### REPLAY-INV-23
Replay cursor state is versioned.

### REPLAY-INV-24
Replay divergence identifies the earliest detected mismatch.

### REPLAY-INV-25
A divergence does not automatically imply root cause.

### REPLAY-INV-26
Unavailable variables remain explicitly unavailable.

### REPLAY-INV-27
Replay source mapping uses stable semantic identities.

### REPLAY-INV-28
Async/task state is correlated using compiler/runtime metadata.

### REPLAY-INV-29
Replay crash correlation references AXCRASH rather than duplicating crash semantics.

### REPLAY-INV-30
Replay profiling correlation references AXPROFILER rather than replacing it.

### REPLAY-INV-31
Replay does not become a general-purpose telemetry system.

### REPLAY-INV-32
Remote replay artifacts require explicit authorization.

### REPLAY-INV-33
Sensitive recorded data can be excluded or redacted.

### REPLAY-INV-34
Artifact integrity is validated before replay.

### REPLAY-INV-35
Cross-architecture replay is rejected unless an explicit compatible replay model exists.

### REPLAY-INV-36
Release binaries have no mandatory replay overhead when replay is disabled.

### REPLAY-INV-37
Recording resource usage is bounded.

### REPLAY-INV-38
AI-visible replay information preserves provenance.

### REPLAY-INV-39
AXTEST can deterministically verify record/replay behavior.

### REPLAY-INV-40
Every conforming implementation satisfies all mandatory replay invariants.

# 1. Purpose

AXDIFF is the canonical difference-analysis subsystem of Axiom.

Its purpose is to answer:

> **What exactly changed between artifact A and artifact B, and what does that change mean?**

It must support multiple comparison layers:

```text
SOURCE
  ↓
AST / SEMANTIC MODEL
  ↓
HIR / MIR / IR
  ↓
OBJECT
  ↓
BINARY
  ↓
ABI/API
  ↓
DEBUG
  ↓
CRASH
  ↓
REPLAY
  ↓
PROFILE
```

The central architectural principle is:

```text
byte difference ≠ semantic difference
semantic difference ≠ ABI difference
ABI difference ≠ behavioral difference
```

AXDIFF therefore provides multiple explicit diff levels rather than one generic binary comparison algorithm.

---

```text

                AXMERGE

```

AXMERGE phải có khả năng hiểu:

- source;

# 2. Nguyên tắc thiết kế bất biến

## MERGE-PRINCIPLE-01 — Three-way là mô hình chuẩn

Mọi semantic merge chính thức phải có:

```text
BASE
LEFT
RIGHT
```

Two-way merge chỉ là compatibility mode.

---

## MERGE-PRINCIPLE-02 — Không được đoán âm thầm

Nếu engine không đủ bằng chứng:

```text
UNKNOWN
```

phải được giữ là `UNKNOWN`.

Không được biến:

```text
unknown
```

thành:

```text
unchanged
```

và không được tự chọn LEFT/RIGHT.

---

## MERGE-PRINCIPLE-03 — Semantic trước textual

Thứ tự ưu tiên:

```text
Symbol Identity
      ↓
Semantic Structure
      ↓
AST
      ↓
Token
      ↓
Text
```

Textual merge chỉ là fallback.

---

## MERGE-PRINCIPLE-04 — SymbolId được ưu tiên tuyệt đối

Nếu BASE, LEFT, RIGHT cùng chứa:

```text
SymbolId = S123
```

thì đây là cùng một symbol trừ khi metadata chứng minh artifact không tương thích.

---

## MERGE-PRINCIPLE-05 — Same change chỉ merge một lần

Nếu:

```text
BASE:  x = 10
LEFT:  x = 20
RIGHT: x = 20
```

kết quả:

```text
x = 20
```

không phải conflict.

---

## MERGE-PRINCIPLE-06 — Independent change tự động hợp nhất

```text
BASE:
a = 1
b = 2

LEFT:
a = 10
b = 2

RIGHT:
a = 1
b = 20
```

→

```text
a = 10
b = 20
```

---

## MERGE-PRINCIPLE-07 — Overlap semantic phải explicit

```text
BASE:  x = 10
LEFT:  x = 20
RIGHT: x = 30
```

→ conflict.

Không tự chọn `20` hoặc `30`.

```text
enum MergeInputKind {
```

```text
struct MergeInput {
```

# 7. Merge model

Canonical:

```text
Merge(BASE, LEFT, RIGHT, POLICY)
    → MergeResult
```

Pseudo-algorithm:

```text
1. validate BASE/LEFT/RIGHT
2. construct identity index
3. calculate semantic deltas:
       ΔL = Diff(BASE, LEFT)
       ΔR = Diff(BASE, RIGHT)
4. normalize changes
5. detect equivalent changes
6. detect independent changes
7. detect overlapping changes
8. apply non-conflicting changes
9. create explicit conflicts
10. apply only policy-authorized resolutions
11. validate merged semantic model
12. validate API
13. validate ABI
14. validate dependencies
15. emit provenance
16. serialize deterministic result
```

---

# 8. Change representation

```text
enum ChangeKind {
    ADD,
    REMOVE,
    MODIFY,
    RENAME,
    MOVE,
    REORDER,
    TYPE_CHANGE,
    SIGNATURE_CHANGE,
    ATTRIBUTE_CHANGE,
    VISIBILITY_CHANGE,
    EFFECT_CHANGE,
    DEPENDENCY_CHANGE,
    ABI_CHANGE,
    API_CHANGE
}
```

```text
struct MergeChange {
    id: ChangeId

    side: MergeSide
    kind: ChangeKind

    target: SemanticId
    parent: optional<SemanticId>

    before: optional<ValueHash>
    after: optional<ValueHash>

    location: SourceLocation
    provenance: Provenance

    confidence: Confidence
}
```

---

# 9. Identity system

Identity levels:

```text
Level 0: SymbolId
Level 1: DeclarationId
Level 2: TypeId
Level 3: Structural fingerprint
Level 4: Signature fingerprint
Level 5: AST similarity
Level 6: textual similarity
```

Matching must proceed from strongest to weakest.

```text
EXACT
STRUCTURAL
INFERRED
UNKNOWN
```

Every non-exact identity match must record its basis.

---

# 10. Rename detection

Example:

```text
BASE:
fn calculate_total()

LEFT:
fn compute_total()

RIGHT:
fn calculate_total() { ...changed... }
```

AXMERGE must recognize:

```text
RENAME:
calculate_total → compute_total
```

rather than:

```text
REMOVE calculate_total
ADD compute_total
```

provided semantic identity evidence is sufficient.

If rename confidence is insufficient:

```text
CONFLICT_RENAME_IDENTITY
```

must be generated rather than silently assuming identity.

---

# 11. Move detection

Moving a declaration between modules:

```text
BASE:
module a
    fn foo()

LEFT:
module b
    fn foo()

RIGHT:
module a
    fn foo() { changed }
```

must be represented as:

```text
MOVE(foo, a → b)
MODIFY(foo)
```

and not merely:

```text
REMOVE + ADD
```

---

# 12. Source merge

Source merge hierarchy:

```text
file
 ↓
module
 ↓
declaration
 ↓
member
 ↓
expression
 ↓
token
 ↓
character
```

The engine must descend to a lower level only when higher-level semantic merging cannot resolve the change.

Example:

```text
fn foo() {
    return a + b;
}
```

LEFT changes:

```text
a + c
```

RIGHT changes:

```text
a * b
```

→ expression conflict.

---

# 13. AST merge

AST nodes must be matched using:

```text
NodeId
SymbolId
parent identity
node kind
structural position
semantic fingerprint
```

AST ordering alone must never be the sole identity mechanism.

---

# 14. Function merge

Independent modifications:

```text
BASE:
fn foo(a) {
    x()
}
```

LEFT:

```text
fn foo(a) {
    x()
    y()
}
```

RIGHT:

```text
fn foo(a) {
    z()
    x()
}
```

can be merged if statement insertion positions are non-conflicting.

Conflicting replacement of the same statement produces:

```text
FUNCTION_BODY_CONFLICT
```

---

# 15. Function signature merge

```text
BASE:
fn foo(x: i32) -> i32
```

LEFT:

```text
fn foo(x: i64) -> i32
```

RIGHT:

```text
fn foo(x: i32) -> f32
```

→ two distinct signature modifications.

Result:

```text
CONFLICT_SIGNATURE
```

The engine must not synthesize:

```text
fn foo(x: i64) -> f32
```

automatically.

---

# 16. Struct merge

Example:

```text
BASE:
struct User {
    id: u64
}
```

LEFT:

```text
struct User {
    id: u64
    name: String
}
```

RIGHT:

```text
struct User {
    id: u64
    age: u32
}
```

Result:

```text
struct User {
    id: u64
    name: String
    age: u32
}
```

provided field insertion/layout policy permits it.

---

# 17. Struct same-field conflict

```text
BASE:
name: String

LEFT:
name: SmallString

RIGHT:
name: StringView
```

→

```text
STRUCT_FIELD_TYPE_CONFLICT
```

No automatic type synthesis.

---

# 18. Struct layout

Layout changes require additional ABI analysis.

A source merge may succeed:

```text
struct User {
    id: u64
    age: u32
}
```

but ABI validation may subsequently report:

```text
ABI_LAYOUT_CHANGED
```

This distinction is mandatory.

```text
SOURCE_MERGE_SUCCESS
≠
ABI_COMPATIBILITY_SUCCESS
```

---

# 19. Enum merge

Independent variant additions:

```text
BASE:
enum Color {
    Red
}
```

LEFT:

```text
Red
Green
```

RIGHT:

```text
Red
Blue
```

→

```text
Red
Green
Blue
```

unless explicit discriminants or ordering policies create a collision.

---

# 20. Enum discriminant conflict

```text
BASE:
A = 1
B = 2
```

LEFT:

```text
C = 3
```

RIGHT:

```text
C = 4
```

→ conflict.

No automatic renumbering.

Reason:

Changing discriminants may be an ABI/data-format compatibility break.

---

# 21. Union merge

Union members are identity-bearing fields.

Independent additions may merge.

Conflicting changes to the same member:

```text
BASE:
x: i32

LEFT:
x: i64

RIGHT:
x: f64
```

→ `UNION_MEMBER_CONFLICT`.

---

# 22. Trait merge

Independent associated items merge.

```text
trait Drawable {
    draw()
}
```

LEFT:

```text
draw()
bounds()
```

RIGHT:

```text
draw()
serialize()
```

→

```text
draw()
bounds()
serialize()
```

provided no signature/name collision exists.

---

# 23. Trait implementation conflicts

If both sides introduce incompatible implementations:

```text
impl Drawable for Widget
```

and:

```text
impl Drawable for Widget
```

with different bodies, AXMERGE must report:

```text
DUPLICATE_TRAIT_IMPL_CONFLICT
```

unless the language's coherence rules explicitly permit both.

---

# 24. Generic merge

Generic parameter identity is positional only as a fallback.

Preferred:

```text
GenericParamId
```

Example:

```text
fn map<T>(...)
```

LEFT:

```text
fn map<T, U>(...)
```

RIGHT:

```text
fn map<T>(...) where T: Copy
```

may merge:

```text
fn map<T, U>(...)
where
    T: Copy
```

if the added parameter and constraint are independent.

---

# 25. Generic constraint conflict

```text
BASE:
T

LEFT:
T: Copy

RIGHT:
T: !Copy
```

→ explicit generic constraint conflict.

The engine must not invent a composite constraint unless the language semantic model proves it equivalent.

---

# 26. Attributes/effects

Merge independently:

```text
@inline
@cold
@deprecated
```

but conflicting semantic attributes must be analyzed.

Example:

```text
BASE:
@inline

LEFT:
@noinline

RIGHT:
@inline
```

→ LEFT's modification is not automatically discarded.

Result depends on BASE-relative change:

```text
LEFT = changed
RIGHT = unchanged
```

therefore merged result:

```text
@noinline
```

This is a critical three-way rule.

---

# 27. Visibility merge

```text
BASE:
private fn foo()

LEFT:
public fn foo()

RIGHT:
private fn foo()
```

→ `public`.

But:

```text
LEFT:
public

RIGHT:
internal
```

→ conflict because both changed the same semantic property differently.

---

# 28. Effect merge

Effects are semantic.

Example:

```text
fn foo() -> i32
```

LEFT:

```text
fn foo() throws -> i32
```

RIGHT:

```text
fn foo() async -> i32
```

These are not text-level independent modifications.

AXMERGE must classify:

```text
EFFECT_SET_CONFLICT
```

unless the effect algebra proves composition valid.

---

# 29. Module/import merge

Imports are modeled as sets plus ordering metadata.

```text
BASE:
import A

LEFT:
import B

RIGHT:
import C
```

→

```text
import A
import B
import C
```

Duplicate equivalent imports are coalesced.

Conflicting aliases:

```text
import foo as x
import bar as x
```

→ `IMPORT_ALIAS_CONFLICT`.

---

# 30. Dependency graph

AXMERGE maintains:

```text
Package
   ↓
Module
   ↓
Import
   ↓
Symbol
   ↓
Type
   ↓
Build Target
```

Changes must propagate through this graph.

A local source merge that creates an invalid dependency cycle is not considered a complete successful merge.

---

# 31. Dependency conflict

Example:

```text
BASE:
foo = 1.4

LEFT:
foo = 2.0

RIGHT:
foo = 3.0
```

→

```text
DEPENDENCY_VERSION_CONFLICT
```

unless package constraints prove a common valid version.

---

# 32. Feature conflict

```text
BASE:
foo { default }

LEFT:
foo { gpu }

RIGHT:
foo { no-gpu }
```

→ explicit feature conflict.

---

# 33. Lockfile merge

Lockfiles are structured artifacts.

They must not be merged as arbitrary text.

Merge:

```text
package identity
version
source
checksum
dependencies
features
target
```

independently.

Checksum mismatch must produce:

```text
LOCKFILE_INTEGRITY_CONFLICT
```

---

# 34. API merge

API model:

```text
API
 ├ symbols
 ├ visibility
 ├ signatures
 ├ types
 ├ traits
 ├ constants
 ├ attributes
 └ deprecations
```

AXMERGE must generate an API delta after merging.

Example:

```text
API_REMOVE
API_ADD
API_SIGNATURE_CHANGE
API_VISIBILITY_CHANGE
API_TYPE_CHANGE
```

API merge success does not imply backward compatibility.

---

# 35. ABI merge

AXMERGE delegates ABI truth to AXABI.

Pipeline:

```text
Merged Semantic Model
        ↓
AXABI validation
        ↓
AbiCompatibilityReport
```

Potential results:

```text
ABI_COMPATIBLE
ABI_SOURCE_COMPATIBLE
ABI_BREAKING
ABI_INCOMPARABLE
ABI_UNKNOWN
```

AXMERGE never silently labels `UNKNOWN` as compatible.

---

# 36. Binary merge boundary

Native binaries are **not source merge artifacts**.

Do not attempt:

```text
LEFT.exe + RIGHT.exe → MERGED.exe
```

as the normal model.

Instead:

```text
LEFT source
RIGHT source
BASE source
       ↓
    AXMERGE
       ↓
merged source
       ↓
AXCOMPILER
       ↓
AXLINKER
       ↓
new binary
```

AXBINARY/AXDIFF can compare resulting binaries.

---

# 37. Object artifact policy

Object files may be inspected for merge planning, but native object binaries are normally rebuilt.

AXMERGE may merge:

```text
build configuration
source metadata
dependency metadata
semantic artifact metadata
```

but not arbitrarily splice machine code.

---

# 38. Generated artifact policy

Every generated artifact must declare:

```text
GeneratedPolicy {
    source_of_truth
    generator
    generator_version
    regeneration_command
    merge_policy
}
```

Possible policies:

```text
REGENERATE
MERGE_STRUCTURED
KEEP_IF_IDENTICAL
MANUAL
FORBID
```

Default:

```text
REGENERATE
```

for compiler-generated outputs.

---

# 39. Debug metadata

Debug information is derived from source/build state.

Therefore:

```text
source merge
      ↓
recompile
      ↓
new debug info
```

is preferred.

Manual merging of stale line tables must not become source truth.

---

# 41. Conflict model

```text
struct MergeConflict {
    id: ConflictId

    kind: ConflictKind
    severity: ConflictSeverity

    target: SemanticId

    base: ConflictValue
    left: ConflictValue
    right: ConflictValue

    evidence: ConflictEvidence

    resolution_state: ResolutionState

    provenance: Provenance
}
```

Severity:

```text
INFO
WARNING
ERROR
FATAL
```

# 42. Deterministic ConflictId

Conflict ID must be derived from canonical input:

```text
hash(
    schema_version,
    base_identity,
    left_identity,
    right_identity,
    target_identity,
    conflict_kind,
    normalized_values
)
```

No random UUID may determine semantic conflict identity.

---

# 43. Conflict evidence

```text
struct ConflictEvidence {
    identity_basis
    base_change
    left_change
    right_change

    source_locations
    semantic_paths

    confidence
    affected_symbols
    affected_dependencies
}
```

This allows IDE and AI systems to explain *why* a conflict exists.

---

# 44. Auto-resolvable conflict

Some conflicts are technically represented but policy can resolve them safely.

Examples:

```text
duplicate identical import
same annotation added twice
same field addition
same formatting change
same semantic rename
```

Resolution must still be recorded.

---

# 45. Resolution model

```text
enum ResolutionKind {
    TAKE_BASE,
    TAKE_LEFT,
    TAKE_RIGHT,
    COMBINE,
    EDIT,
    REJECT_CHANGE,
    RENAME,
    MOVE,
    REORDER,
    REGENERATE,
    DEFER
}
```

```text
struct MergeResolution {
    conflict_id: ConflictId
    kind: ResolutionKind

    value: optional<Value>
    resolver: ResolutionSource

    justification: optional<String>
}
```

---

# 46. Resolution provenance

```text
enum ResolutionSource {
    AUTOMATIC,
    USER,
    POLICY,
    SCRIPT,
    AI_PROPOSAL
}
```

`AI_PROPOSAL` is never equivalent to `USER`.

An AI-generated resolution must remain pending until explicitly accepted.

---

# 47. AI-assisted merge

Architecture:

```text
AXMERGE
   ↓
Conflict Context
   ↓
AI Proposal
   ↓
Candidate Resolution
   ↓
Human / Policy Acceptance
   ↓
AXMERGE
```

AI may:

- explain conflicts;
- propose code;
- identify likely rename;
- suggest dependency resolution;
- suggest API-compatible changes;
- summarize affected symbols.

AI may not:

- silently alter files;
- mark unresolved conflicts as resolved;
- suppress ABI conflicts;
- suppress dependency conflicts;
- execute arbitrary code.

---

# 48. Merge policy

```text
struct MergePolicy {
    identity_policy
    rename_policy
    move_policy

    api_policy
    abi_policy
```

# 49. Unknown policy

Allowed:


```text

```

Never:


as a default.

For declarations/fields/variants:

```text
 ├ RightNode
 │
 ├ ChangeNode

 ├ ConflictNode
 └ ResolutionNode
```

```text
DERIVES_FROM
MODIFIES
DEPENDS_ON
CONFLICTS_WITH
RESOLVES
PRESERVES
REPLACES
```

# 52. Merge plan

```text
struct MergePlan {
```

```text
enum MergeOperation {

    Remove
    Modify
    Rename
    Move
    Reorder

    ResolveConflict
```

```text
      ↓
update function foo
      ↓
update trait impl
      ↓
update API
      ↓
validate ABI
```

# 56. Clean vs resolved

```text
CLEAN
```

means no conflict required resolution.

```text
RESOLVED
```

means conflicts existed but every conflict now has an accepted resolution.

# 57. Partial merge

AXMERGE may produce:

```text
PARTIAL
```

for IDE preview.

Same:

```text
BASE
LEFT
RIGHT
```

must produce the same:

```text
merged source
semantic model
conflict IDs
provenance
result hash
```

# 59. Formatting

Preferred:

```text
semantic merge
    ↓
canonical source
    ↓
AXFORMAT
```

rather than treating whitespace differences as meaningful semantic changes.

---

# 60. Text conflict markers

Traditional:

```text
<<<<<<< LEFT
=======
>>>>>>> RIGHT
```

are presentation only.

# 61. AXCODEEDITOR integration

AXCODEEDITOR receives:

# 62. AXIDE integration

AXIDE owns:

```text

conflict navigation
resolution UI
preview
branch/worktree state
save/apply lifecycle
```

AXMERGE owns:

```text
what identities match
what merge is semantically valid
```

```text
merged semantic model
        ↓
AXDOC
        ↓
new API documentation
```

```text

API removals
signature changes
deprecation changes
```

but does not resolve semantic conflicts.

# 64. AXTEST integration

AXTEST must test:

```text
source merge
AST merge
semantic merge
API merge
ABI validation
dependency merge
generated artifact policy
conflict serialization
resolution
determinism
```

# 65. Build integration

AXBUILD receives:

```text
MergeResult
```

only after:

```text
semantic validation
dependency validation
policy validation
```

Then:

```text

 ↓
AXCOMPILER
 ↓
AXLINKER
```

# 66. Incremental merge

For large projects:

```text
changed files
      ↓
changed semantic nodes
      ↓
affected dependency closure
      ↓
partial merge
```

Unchanged subgraphs may be reused.

Cache key:

```text
hash(
    base_node_hash,
    left_node_hash,
    right_node_hash,
    policy_hash,
    schema_version
)
```

# 67. Merge cache

```text
MergeCacheEntry {
    key
    result_hash
    merged_node
    conflicts
    provenance
    schema_version
}
```

# 68. Parallelism

Independent merge graph components may run concurrently.

Constraint:

```text
parallel execution
      ↓
canonical deterministic commit order
```

No race may affect final output.

---

# 69. Large-project performance

Target complexity:

```text
O(N + C)
```

for mostly-independent semantic nodes, where:

- `N` = number of relevant semantic nodes;
- `C` = number of detected change relationships.

Avoid:

```text
O(N²)
```

global pairwise matching.

Use:

```text
SymbolId index
signature index
structural hash index
module index
dependency index
```

---

# 70. Memory model

AXMERGE should use immutable/shared semantic snapshots.

Conceptually:

```text
BASE ──────────────┐
LEFT ──────────────┼→ shared semantic graph
RIGHT ─────────────┘
                         ↓
                   persistent nodes
```

Do not duplicate entire projects merely to merge them.

---

# 71. No execution

AXMERGE must never execute:

- source code;
- build scripts;
- package scripts;
- macros with arbitrary execution;
- generated programs;
- user commands.

Any required semantic information must come from trusted artifacts or AXCOMPILER services.

---

# 72. Macro/generated semantics

If a macro's expansion is required for identity analysis:

```text

```

may be consumed.

AXMERGE itself must not execute the macro.

---

# 73. Security

Untrusted merge inputs must be treated as hostile.

Protection against:

```text
path traversal
resource exhaustion
malformed AST
hash collision abuse
deep nesting
cyclic metadata
oversized conflict payload
malformed dependency graph
malicious generated metadata
```

Limits:

```text
max_nodes
max_depth
max_file_size
max_conflicts
max_dependency_edges
max_memory
max_time
```

---

# 74. Provenance

Every merged node must be attributable:

```text
BASE
LEFT
RIGHT
BOTH_SAME
COMBINED
RESOLVED
GENERATED
POLICY
```

Example:

```text
field name
    provenance = LEFT

field age
    provenance = RIGHT

field id
    provenance = BASE

field address
    provenance = COMBINED
```

```text
SemanticId
```

instead of raw pointers.

# 81. Serialization

`.axmerge` must contain:

# 82. Streaming

# 83. Remote merge

Remote AXMERGE service may accept:

Authentication and authorization belong to platform/security layers.

# 84. Reproducibility

Given:

```text
B
L
R
P
S
```

where:

- B = BASE identity;
- L = LEFT identity;
- R = RIGHT identity;
- P = policy;
- S = schema;

then:

```text
Merge(B,L,R,P,S)
```

must produce the same canonical result.

---

# 85. Three-way correctness properties

AXTEST must verify:

### Identity preservation

If a symbol is unchanged:

```text
SymbolId(result) = SymbolId(BASE)
```

---

### Same-change coalescing

```text
ΔL == ΔR
```

→ one change.

---

### Independent-change composition

```text
ΔL ∩ ΔR = ∅
```

→ both applied.

---

### Conflict preservation

```text
ΔL(x) != ΔR(x)
```

on the same semantic property → explicit conflict.

---

### No silent loss

Every non-base change must be:

```text
APPLIED
REJECTED
CONFLICTED
```

and never disappear without provenance.

---

# 86. Rename correctness

Tests:

```text
rename only
rename + modify
rename on both sides identically
different rename
rename vs remove
rename vs modify
rename vs move
```

---

# 87. Move correctness

Tests:

```text
move only
move + modify
same move
different move
move vs delete
move vs rename
cross-module move
cross-package move
```

---

# 88. Struct correctness

Tests:

```text
add independent fields
remove independent fields
same field modification
different type modification
field rename
field reorder
layout-sensitive change
visibility change
default-value change
```

---

# 89. Enum correctness

Tests:

```text
variant additions
variant removals
same discriminant
different discriminant
variant rename
variant payload modification
ordering change
```

---

# 90. Generic correctness

Tests:

```text
parameter addition
parameter removal
constraint addition
constraint conflict
default parameter
variance-related semantic changes
generic rename
generic reorder
```

---

# 91. Dependency correctness

Tests:

```text
independent dependency additions
same version
different versions
compatible version ranges
incompatible ranges
feature conflict
target-specific dependency
lockfile checksum conflict
cycle introduction
```

---

# 92. API correctness

AXTEST must compare:

```text
merged API
expected API
AXDIFF API diff
```

and ensure no API change is lost.

---

# 93. ABI correctness

After merge:

```text
AXABI
   ↓
ABI report
```

must be reproducible.

ABI-breaking changes must remain visible even when source merge is clean.

---

# 94. Binary correctness

Workflow:

```text
BASE → compile → BINARY_BASE
LEFT → compile → BINARY_LEFT
RIGHT → compile → BINARY_RIGHT

MERGED → compile → BINARY_MERGED
```

Then:

```text
AXDIFF
```

compares artifacts.

AXMERGE itself does not infer correctness from binary bytes.

---

# 95. Crash/profile/replay boundary

These artifacts are diagnostic evidence.

They are not normally mergeable source state.

AXMERGE may preserve references:

```text
CrashArtifactId
ProfileArtifactId
ReplayArtifactId
```

but does not combine execution histories as if they were source.

---

# 96. Deterministic diagnostics

Diagnostics ordering:

```text
severity
semantic path
source location
ConflictId
```

must be deterministic.

---

# 97. Conflict navigation

Each conflict must expose:

```text
base range
left range
right range
semantic target
dependency impact
API impact
ABI impact
resolution state
```

This gives AXIDE enough information to navigate directly to the cause.

---

# 98. Semantic impact analysis

For every conflict:

```text
Conflict
   ↓
affected symbols
   ↓
affected modules
   ↓
affected APIs
   ↓
affected ABI
   ↓
affected targets
```

Impact is advisory unless validated by AXCOMPILER/AXABI.

---

# 99. Merge modes

```text
MERGE_SOURCE
MERGE_AST
MERGE_SEMANTIC
MERGE_API
MERGE_ABI
MERGE_DEPENDENCY
MERGE_BUILD
MERGE_METADATA
MERGE_COMBINED
```

`MERGE_COMBINED` is the default full-project mode.

---

# 100. Two-way mode

Two-way:

```text
CURRENT
OTHER
```

must be internally converted into:

```text
BASE = CURRENT
LEFT = CURRENT
RIGHT = OTHER
```

or equivalent explicit semantics.

The UI must clearly indicate that no historical base exists.

---

# 101. Merge strategy

```text
SEMANTIC_FIRST
AST_FIRST
TOKEN_FIRST
TEXT_FIRST
API_FIRST
DEPENDENCY_FIRST
```

Default:

```text
SEMANTIC_FIRST
```

Fallback:

```text
AST → TOKEN → TEXT
```

---

# 102. Formatting-only changes

Formatting differences should be classified separately:

```text
FORMAT_ONLY
SEMANTIC_CHANGE
```

If one side reformats and another changes semantics, semantic changes must survive formatting normalization.

---

# 103. Comment merge

Comments have source identity where available.

Independent comment additions merge.

Conflicting edits to the same comment may be represented as textual conflicts without contaminating semantic symbol identity.

---

# 104. Documentation comments

Documentation attached to a symbol belongs to that symbol.

Thus:

```text
SymbolId
   └── DocNode
```

Two independent documentation edits can merge separately from implementation changes.

---

# 105. Source ownership model

AXMERGE must not introduce ownership semantics into Axiom source.

It consumes the language's existing semantic model.

Memory/lifetime validation remains AXCOMPILER's responsibility.

---

# 106. Compiler integration

After merge:

```text
AXMERGE
   ↓
AXCOMPILER.parse
   ↓
AXCOMPILER.resolve
   ↓
AXCOMPILER.typecheck
   ↓
AXCOMPILER.lower
```

A semantic merge is not considered build-ready until the relevant compiler validation passes.

---

# 107. Error recovery

Malformed input:

```text
ERROR_INPUT_INVALID
```

must not be transformed into a merge conflict.

Distinguish:

```text
invalid input
```

from:

```text
valid but conflicting input
```

---

# 108. Version compatibility

If:

```text
BASE schema != LEFT schema
```

AXMERGE may normalize versions only when a declared migration exists.

Otherwise:

```text
SCHEMA_INCOMPATIBLE
```

---

# 109. Artifact identity

Each input receives:

```text
ArtifactId
ContentHash
SemanticHash
TargetIdentity
AbiIdentity
SchemaVersion
```

This prevents accidental merging of artifacts from incompatible targets.

---

# 110. Cross-target merge

Source can be merged across targets when target-independent.

Example:

```text
Windows PE64
Linux ELF64
```

may share source semantic state.

Target-specific sections must be represented separately:

```text
TARGET_CONDITIONAL
```

rather than accidentally merged.

---

# 111. Conditional compilation

Example:

```text
if target == windows {
    ...
}
```

and:

```text
if target == linux {
    ...
}
```

must be merged by conditional semantic identity.

AXMERGE must not treat mutually exclusive target branches as conflicts merely because they occupy similar source locations.

---

# 112. Build configuration merge

Structured merge:

```text
targets
sources
defines
features
dependencies
compiler_options
linker_options
resources
signing
packaging
```

Conflicting compiler/linker flags must be explicit.

---

# 113. Signing metadata

Signing credentials/secrets must never become merge content.

Only public metadata/policy may be represented.

Example:

```text
signing_required = true
certificate_identity = X
```

Secrets remain external.

---

# 114. Resource merge

Structured resources may support:

```text
ADD
REMOVE
MODIFY
REPLACE
```

Binary resource payloads should normally use:

```text
identity + replacement
```

not byte-level semantic synthesis.

---

# 115. Localization merge

String tables are keyed by stable identifiers:

```text
StringId
Locale
Variant
```

Two locales can merge independently.

Same locale/key with different values produces conflict.

---

# 116. AI metadata merge

Axiom AI metadata:

```text
semantic descriptions
symbol summaries
constraints
examples
provenance
```

must merge by `SymbolId`.

Generated AI descriptions are never allowed to overwrite human-authored normative metadata without policy authorization.

---

# 117. Trust levels

```text
NORMATIVE
COMPILER_DERIVED
TEST_VERIFIED
USER_AUTHORED
AI_PROPOSED
EXTERNAL
```

When evidence conflicts, provenance is preserved rather than silently choosing based on trust ranking.

---

# 118. Merge result trust

Result fields should expose:

```text
verified
unverified
conflicted
inferred
```

An inferred identity must never look like an exact identity to AXIDE or AI consumers.

---

# 119. Canonical semantic merge tree

```text
MergedProject
 ├ modules
 │   ├ declarations
 │   │   ├ functions
 │   │   ├ structs
 │   │   ├ enums
 │   │   ├ unions
 │   │   └ traits
 │   │
 │   └ imports
 │
 ├ dependencies
 ├ build
 ├ metadata
 └ provenance
```

---

# 120. Core invariants

### MERGE-INV-01
Three-way merge uses BASE/LEFT/RIGHT.

### MERGE-INV-02
Same semantic change on both sides is applied once.

### MERGE-INV-03
Independent semantic changes are preserved.

### MERGE-INV-04
Conflicting changes produce explicit conflicts.

### MERGE-INV-05
No unresolved conflict may be silently discarded.

### MERGE-INV-06
Exact SymbolId identity is preserved.

### MERGE-INV-07
Inferred identity carries provenance.

### MERGE-INV-08
Rename is represented as rename when identity evidence permits.

### MERGE-INV-09
Move is represented as move when identity evidence permits.

### MERGE-INV-10
Struct field conflicts are explicit.

### MERGE-INV-11
Enum discriminant conflicts are explicit.

### MERGE-INV-12
Trait implementation conflicts are explicit.

### MERGE-INV-13
Generic constraint conflicts are explicit.

### MERGE-INV-14
Effect conflicts are explicit.

### MERGE-INV-15
API changes are separately reported.

### MERGE-INV-16
ABI validation is delegated to AXABI.

### MERGE-INV-17
Unknown ABI compatibility is never assumed compatible.

### MERGE-INV-18
Dependency conflicts are structurally represented.

### MERGE-INV-19
Lockfile integrity conflicts are explicit.

### MERGE-INV-20
Generated artifacts follow explicit generation policy.

### MERGE-INV-21
Native binaries are normally rebuilt, not byte-merged.

### MERGE-INV-22
No arbitrary code executes during merge.

### MERGE-INV-23
AI proposals are not automatic resolutions.

### MERGE-INV-24
Every resolution has provenance.

### MERGE-INV-25
Conflict IDs are deterministic.

### MERGE-INV-26
Merge plans are deterministic.

### MERGE-INV-27
Serialized `.axmerge` artifacts are deterministic.

### MERGE-INV-28
Parallel execution cannot alter semantic result.

### MERGE-INV-29
Merge cache keys include policy/schema identity.

### MERGE-INV-30
Invalid input is distinct from semantic conflict.

### MERGE-INV-31
Partial merge is never implicitly build-ready.

### MERGE-INV-32
Formatting does not alter semantic identity.

### MERGE-INV-33
Comments cannot destroy declaration identity.

### MERGE-INV-34
Cross-target conditional branches remain target-aware.

### MERGE-INV-35
Build configuration conflicts are explicit.

### MERGE-INV-36
Signing secrets never enter merge artifacts.

### MERGE-INV-37
Provenance survives serialization.

### MERGE-INV-38
Merged source must be compiler-valid before build approval.

### MERGE-INV-39
Merge result must be reproducible from its canonical inputs.

### MERGE-INV-40
AXMERGE never silently invents semantic intent.

```text
   ↓
```

Every successful merge should optionally generate:


containing affected:

```text

integration tests
API tests

target tests
```

## PATCH-PRINCIPLE-02 — Patch không phụ thuộc tuyệt đối vào dòng

Một patch hợp lệ phải tiếp tục có khả năng áp dụng sau khi:

- thêm dòng phía trên;

## PATCH-PRINCIPLE-03 — Patch phải có precondition

Patch không được chỉ chứa:

```text
old → new
```

mà phải có:

```text
target identity
expected state
operation
new state
```

Ví dụ:

```text
target = S123
expected_hash = H1
operation = MODIFY
new_hash = H2
```

Nếu target hiện tại có hash `H3`:

```text
PATCH_PRECONDITION_FAILED
```

# 31. Undo

Undo có thể được biểu diễn bằng inverse patch.

```text
P
↓
apply
↓
P⁻¹
```

AXEDITOR vẫn có quyền quản lý UI undo stack.

---

# 32. Patch inversion

Mỗi invertible operation:

```text
ADD       ↔ REMOVE
MODIFY    ↔ MODIFY(reverse)
RENAME    ↔ RENAME(reverse)
MOVE      ↔ MOVE(reverse)
REORDER   ↔ REORDER(reverse)
```

Không phải mọi patch đều invertible.

Ví dụ:

```text
REGENERATE
```

có thể không có inverse nếu generator state không được lưu.

---

# 33. Inverse patch

```text
invert(P) → P_inverse
```

Yêu cầu:

```text
apply(P)
apply(P_inverse)
```

phải khôi phục semantic state ban đầu nếu không có external mutation.

---

# 34. Patch composition

```text
P1
 ↓
P2
 ↓
P3
```

có thể compose:

```text
compose(P1, P2) → P12
compose(P12, P3) → P123
```

---

# 35. Composition correctness

Nếu:

```text
S1 = apply(P1, S0)
S2 = apply(P2, S1)
```

thì:

```text
apply(compose(P1,P2), S0) = S2
```

với điều kiện preconditions tương thích.

---

# 36. Composition conflict

Nếu:

```text
P1:
x = 10 → 20

P2:
x = 10 → 30
```

thì:

```text
compose(P1,P2)
```

phải tạo conflict.

Không được chọn 20 hoặc 30 âm thầm.

---

# 37. Patch rebase

Rebase:

```text
Patch P
   ↓
Base A
   ↓
New Base B
```

Mục tiêu:

```text
P' applies to B
```

và giữ nguyên semantic intent của P.

---

# 38. Rebase algorithm

```text
rebase(P, A → B)
```

Pipeline:

```text
1. identify P targets
2. diff A → B
3. transform P against Δ(A,B)
4. preserve SymbolId
5. update positions
6. validate preconditions
7. emit conflicts if intent cannot be preserved
```

---

# 39. Rebase example

BASE:

```text
fn foo()
fn bar()
```

Patch:

```text
modify foo
```

New base:

```text
fn new_function()
fn foo()
fn bar()
```

Patch vẫn áp dụng vào `foo` vì identity không thay đổi.

Line-based patch có thể thất bại; semantic patch không.

---

# 40. Rebase rename

BASE:

```text
foo()
```

Patch:

```text
modify foo
```

New base:

```text
compute()
```

Nếu `foo → compute` được AXDIFF/semantic identity xác nhận:

```text
rebase(P)
```

sẽ chuyển target:

```text
foo → compute
```

nhưng giữ nguyên `SymbolId`.

Nếu identity không chắc chắn:

```text
REBASE_IDENTITY_CONFLICT
```

tìm patch `P'` sao cho:

```text
then Q
```

tương đương về semantic state với:

```text
apply(Q)
then P'
```

nếu hai patch có thể commute.

# 99. Algebraic tests

### Identity

```text
apply(identity_patch, S) = S
```

### Inverse

```text
apply(invert(P), apply(P,S)) = S
```

### Composition

```text
apply(compose(P,Q),S)
=
apply(Q,apply(P,S))
```

### Idempotence

Patch không có side effects ngoài semantic state phải thỏa:

```text
apply(P, apply(P,S))
```

→ conflict/stale hoặc semantic equivalent theo policy; không được tạo duplicate unintended changes.

thì `S2` phải giữ semantic intent của P tương ứng với những thay đổi của A→B.

Không yêu cầu byte-for-byte equality.

# 114. 40 invariants

### PATCH-INV-01
Patch IDs are deterministic.

### PATCH-INV-02
Semantic identity has priority over source location.

### PATCH-INV-03
Every mutating operation has an explicit target.

### PATCH-INV-04
Every destructive operation has an expected state.

### PATCH-INV-05
Precondition failure never silently applies the patch.

### PATCH-INV-06
Patch application is atomic by default.

### PATCH-INV-07
Rename preserves SymbolId.

### PATCH-INV-08
Move preserves SymbolId.

### PATCH-INV-09
Independent operations may be parallelized.

### PATCH-INV-10
Parallel execution cannot alter result ordering.

### PATCH-INV-11
Add operations cannot silently overwrite an existing semantic identity.

### PATCH-INV-12
Remove cannot delete a changed target under strict policy.

### PATCH-INV-13
Modify validates expected state.

### PATCH-INV-14
Reorder does not alter semantic identity.

### PATCH-INV-15
Formatting does not alter semantic identity.

### PATCH-INV-16
Equivalent operations may be normalized.

### PATCH-INV-17
Semantic equality is distinct from textual equality.

### PATCH-INV-18
Inverse patches preserve provenance.

### PATCH-INV-19
Non-invertible operations explicitly report non-invertibility.

### PATCH-INV-20
Composition cannot silently resolve conflicting writes.

### PATCH-INV-21
Rebase preserves identity when identity evidence permits.

### PATCH-INV-22
Ambiguous rebase produces explicit conflict.

### PATCH-INV-23
Transformation cannot discard a semantic change silently.

### PATCH-INV-24
API-affecting patches are explicitly marked.

### PATCH-INV-25
ABI-affecting patches are explicitly marked.

### PATCH-INV-26
ABI compatibility is delegated to AXABI.

### PATCH-INV-27
Dependency patches preserve package identity/integrity metadata.

### PATCH-INV-28
Generated artifacts obey declared generation policy.

### PATCH-INV-29
Binary patches cannot masquerade as source patches.

### PATCH-INV-30
AI-generated patches remain proposals until accepted.

### PATCH-INV-31
AI cannot bypass validation.

### PATCH-INV-32
Every applied operation has provenance.

### PATCH-INV-33
Persistent mutation occurs only through explicit apply/commit paths.

### PATCH-INV-34
Patch serialization is canonical.

### PATCH-INV-35
Deserialization validates schema before semantic interpretation.

### PATCH-INV-36
Untrusted patches cannot trigger arbitrary code execution.

### PATCH-INV-37
Resource limits are enforced.

### PATCH-INV-38
Cache keys include semantic/schema/policy identity.

### PATCH-INV-39
Equivalent canonical patches produce identical semantic hashes.

### PATCH-INV-40
AXPATCH never silently invents semantic intent.

# 130. 40 invariants

### HISTORY-INV-01
Revision graph is a DAG.

### HISTORY-INV-02
RevisionId is deterministic.

### HISTORY-INV-03
Revision semantic content is immutable.

### HISTORY-INV-04
Parent relationships are explicit.

### HISTORY-INV-05
Merge revisions preserve all parents.

### HISTORY-INV-06
Revision identity does not depend on timestamp.

### HISTORY-INV-07
Symbol lineage prefers SymbolId.

### HISTORY-INV-08
Inferred lineage is explicitly marked.

### HISTORY-INV-09
Rename preserves lineage when identity is preserved.

### HISTORY-INV-10
Move preserves lineage when identity is preserved.

### HISTORY-INV-11
One-to-many symbol transformations are representable.

### HISTORY-INV-12
Many-to-one symbol transformations are representable.

### HISTORY-INV-13
Remove does not erase historical lineage.

### HISTORY-INV-14
Reappearance does not imply identity automatically.

### HISTORY-INV-15
Property-level history is supported.

### HISTORY-INV-16
API history is distinct from source history.

### HISTORY-INV-17
ABI history is distinct from API history.

### HISTORY-INV-18
AXABI remains ABI authority.

### HISTORY-INV-19
Dependency history is structurally represented.

### HISTORY-INV-20
Patch history references canonical AXPATCH identities.

### HISTORY-INV-21
Merge history references AXMERGE provenance.

### HISTORY-INV-22
AXDIFF provides difference analysis.

### HISTORY-INV-23
AXHISTORY does not execute source code.

### HISTORY-INV-24
AI cannot silently rewrite history.

### HISTORY-INV-25
AI proposals are distinct from accepted changes.

### HISTORY-INV-26
Derived indexes are not canonical truth.

### HISTORY-INV-27
Indexes can be deterministically rebuilt.

### HISTORY-INV-28
Partial history never implies absence of history.

### HISTORY-INV-29
Missing ancestors are represented as unknown.

### HISTORY-INV-30
Historical compiler validity is distinct from current validity.

### HISTORY-INV-31
Revision target/ABI identity is preserved.

### HISTORY-INV-32
Canonical serialization is deterministic.

### HISTORY-INV-33
Query ordering is deterministic.

### HISTORY-INV-34
History compaction preserves semantic lineage.

### HISTORY-INV-35
Revert uses semantic patch semantics.

### HISTORY-INV-36
Cherry-pick uses patch/rebase semantics.

### HISTORY-INV-37
Untrusted history is resource-limited.

### HISTORY-INV-38
Malformed cycles are rejected.

### HISTORY-INV-39
Provenance survives serialization.

### HISTORY-INV-40
AXHISTORY never invents historical facts absent from its evidence.

# 1. Mục tiêu

`AXVCS` là lớp **repository và synchronization** native của Axiom.

Nó không thay thế:

- `AXHISTORY` — semantic history;
- `AXMERGE` — semantic merge;
- `AXPATCH` — patch application;
- `AXDIFF` — difference analysis.

AXVCS cung cấp:

```text
repository
object storage
refs
branch/tag transport
commit storage
fetch/push/pull
remote synchronization
CAS
packfiles
partial clone
sparse checkout
integrity
locking
authentication boundary
```

Kiến trúc tổng thể:

```text
                    AXVCS
                      │
       ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
       ▼              ▼              ▼
 Repository       Object Store    Transport
       │              │              │
       ▼              ▼              ▼
   AXHISTORY         CAS         Remote
       │
       ├── AXMERGE
       ├── AXPATCH
       └── AXDIFF
```

---

# 2. Boundary

AXVCS **owns**:

```text
Repository
Object
ObjectStore
Ref
BranchRef
TagRef
RemoteRef
Pack
Transport
Fetch
Push
Pull
Clone
Integrity
GC
Lock
RepositoryConfig
```

AXVCS **does not own**:

```text
type checking
compiler semantics
source merge
semantic diff
patch semantics
ABI rules
build execution
package resolution
authentication policy
UI
```

# 3. Core design principle

Axiom không thiết kế VCS dựa trên:

```text
file → line → commit
```

mà:

```text
content
   ↓
semantic snapshot
   ↓
revision
   ↓
content-addressed repository
```

Do đó:

```text
AXHISTORY
      ↓
RevisionId
      ↓
AXVCS
      ↓
Object Store
```

Một repository:

```text
Repository {
    id

    config
    refs
    object_store
    remotes
    capabilities
}
```

```text
RepositoryId =
```

```text
enum ObjectKind {
```

Repository có thể khai báo:

```text

```

```text

```

Repository có:

```text

```

trỏ tới:

```text

```

```text

```

AXVCS không coi working tree là semantic truth.

```text
WORKING TREE
     ↓
AXCOMPILER
     ↓
semantic snapshot
     ↓
AXHISTORY
     ↓
```


User có thể commit:

```text

property Y
```

```text

```

Đây là điểm khác biệt quan trọng của AXVCS.

```text
StageSelection {

}
```

Compiler/AXDIFF xác định semantic boundaries.

```text
Working Tree
     ↓
AXCOMPILER
     ↓
Semantic Snapshot
     ↓
AXDIFF
     ↓
Change Set
     ↓
AXPATCH
     ↓
AXHISTORY
     ↓
Revision
     ↓
AXVCS
```

# 25. Commit operation

Conceptual:

```text
commit(
    base_revision,
    working_snapshot,
    selection,
    metadata
)
```

Kết quả:

```text
RevisionId
```

---

# 26. Atomic commit

Commit phải atomic:

```text
either:
    all referenced objects + revision + ref
exist

or:
    repository state remains unchanged
```

Không được tạo branch trỏ vào revision chưa đầy đủ.

---

# 27. Object transaction

```text
ObjectTransaction {
    staged_objects
    expected_refs
    commit()
    abort()
}
```

---

# 28. Ref transaction

Atomic ref update:

```text
RefTransaction {
    expected_old
    new_value
}
```

---

# 29. Compare-and-swap ref

```text
update_ref(
    ref,
    expected_old,
    new_revision
)
```

Nếu current ref khác `expected_old`:

```text
REF_CONFLICT
```

Không overwrite silent.

---

# 30. Concurrent commits

Hai client:

```text
A: R10 → R11
B: R10 → R12
```

cả hai có thể commit local.

Push chỉ thành công khi remote ref vẫn:

```text
R10
```

Nếu remote đã thành:

```text
R11
```

B phải integrate.

---

# 31. Push

```text
LOCAL
  │
  ├── discover remote state
  │
  ├── compute object closure
  │
  ├── send missing objects
  │
  ├── validate
  │
  └── atomic ref update
       ↓
REMOTE
```

---

# 32. Push must not mutate source

Push chỉ:

```text
transfer objects
update remote refs
```

Không tự sửa working tree.

---

# 33. Fetch

```text
REMOTE
  ↓
advertised refs
  ↓
object negotiation
  ↓
missing objects
  ↓
LOCAL object store
  ↓
remote-tracking refs
```

---

# 34. Remote-tracking refs

Ví dụ:

```text
refs/remotes/origin/main
```

là local reference.

Nó không tự động thay đổi local branch.

---

# 35. Pull

Canonical:

```text
fetch
  ↓
integrate
  ↓
merge/rebase policy
```

AXVCS fetches.

AXMERGE performs semantic merge.

AXPATCH performs rebase/application where appropriate.

---

# 36. Pull must not silently merge

Repository policy:

```text
pull_policy:
    FAST_FORWARD
    MERGE
    REBASE
    PROMPT
```

Nếu policy không cho phép automatic integration:

```text
PULL_REQUIRES_INTEGRATION
```

---

# 37. Fast-forward

Nếu:

```text
local = R10
remote = R12
R10 ancestor of R12
```

thì:

```text
local → R12
```

không cần merge.

---

# 38. Non-fast-forward

Nếu:

```text
       R11
      /
R10
      \
       R12
```

thì phải:

```text
merge
```

hoặc:

```text
rebase
```

theo policy.

---

# 39. Semantic merge boundary

AXVCS không thực hiện merge semantics.

```text
AXVCS
  ↓
common ancestor
left revision
right revision
  ↓
AXMERGE
```

---

# 40. Merge result

AXMERGE trả:

```text
MergeResult {
    merged_snapshot
    conflicts[]
    resolutions[]
    provenance
```
